title: DeepSeek Lure Using CAPTCHAs To Spread Malware
content:
## Snapshot
Researchers at ThreatLabz have identified a malware campaign that exploits the popularity of the DeepSeek AI chatbot through brand impersonation.

## Description
Cybercriminals are using fake DeepSeek look-alike domains to distribute the Vidar information stealer, targeting users with a fake CAPTCHA page that injects a malicious PowerShell command into their clipboard. When the command is executed, it downloads the Vidar executable, which then steals sensitive data such as credentials, cryptocurrency wallet information, browser cookies, and personal files. The malware specifically searches for data related to cryptocurrency wallets and browser extensions within the victim's file system and registry.

Vidar conceals its command-and-control communication using legitimate services like Telegram and Steam. The campaign uses a malicious website that mimics DeepSeek, registered on January 31, 2025, to lure victims with a fake partner registration prompt. The Vidar malware harvests a wide range of data and uses legitimate platforms to exfiltrate the stolen information to attacker-controlled servers, which include several IP addresses and a publicly accessible Steam community profile.

## Microsoft Analysis and Additional OSINT Context
Cybercriminals frequently exploit the popularity of emerging apps and technologies, such as DeepSeek, by leveraging information stealers that operate on the malware-as-a-service (MaaS) model, like Vidar, to create scalable and flexible campaigns. These campaigns capitalize on user excitement and curiosity surrounding new technologies, using social engineering tactics to trick victims into interacting with malware. The MaaS model enhances the scalability and adaptability of these operations, enabling attackers to easily customize malware payloads, automate distribution, and target a broad range of victims with minimal technical expertise.

[Information stealers](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/2296d491ea381b532b24f2575f9418d4b6723c17b8a1f507d20c2140a75d16d6) are particularly favored in these campaigns because they allow cybercriminals to exfiltrate credentials, session cookies, and system data, facilitating further compromise, identity theft, and unauthorized access to corporate networks. The adaptability of MaaS-based malware ensures that threat actors can swiftly adjust their tactics to align with trending technologies, maximizing infection rates and profitability. As new innovations continue to capture public interest, these malicious campaigns highlight the need for heightened awareness, robust endpoint security, and cautious software sourcing to mitigate the risks posed by opportunistic cyber threats.

## Recommendations
Microsoft recommends the following mitigations to reduce the impact of this threat. Check the recommendations card for the deployment status of monitored mitigations.

- Check your Office 365 email filtering settings to ensure you block spoofed emails, spam, and emails with malware. Use [Microsoft Defender for Office 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/defender-for-office-365?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) for enhanced phishing protection and coverage against new threats and polymorphic variants. Configure Microsoft Defender for Office 365 to [recheck links on click](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/safe-links-about?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) and [delete sent mail](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/zero-hour-auto-purge?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in response to newly acquired threat intelligence. Turn on [safe attachments policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/safe-attachments-policies-configure?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to check attachments to inbound email.
- Encourage users to use Microsoft Edge and other web browsers that support [SmartScreen](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/web-protection-overview?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc), which identifies and blocks malicious websites, including phishing sites, scam sites, and sites that host malware.
- Turn on [cloud-delivered protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/configure-block-at-first-sight-microsoft-defender-antivirus?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in Microsoft Defender Antivirus, or the equivalent for your antivirus product, to cover rapidly evolving attacker tools and techniques. Cloud-based machine learning protections block a majority of new and unknown variants.
- Enforce MFA on all accounts, remove users excluded from MFA, and strictly [require MFA](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/identity-protection/howto-identity-protection-configure-mfa-policy?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) from all devices, in all locations, at all times.
- Enable passwordless authentication methods (for example, Windows Hello, FIDO keys, or Microsoft Authenticator) for accounts that support passwordless. For accounts that still require passwords, use authenticator apps like Microsoft Authenticator for MFA. [Refer to this article](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/authentication/concept-authentication-methods?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) for the different authentication methods and features.
- For MFA that uses authenticator apps, ensure that the app requires a code to be typed in where possible, as many intrusions where MFA was enabled still succeeded due to users clicking “Yes” on the prompt on their phones even when they were not at their [devices](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/authentication/how-to-mfa-number-match?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc). Refer to [this article](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/authentication/concept-authentication-methods?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) for an example.
- Remind employees that enterprise or workplace credentials should not be stored in browsers or password vaults secured with personal credentials. Organizations can turn off password syncing in browser on managed devices using [Group Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/microsoft-edge-enterprise-sync#sync-group-policies?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc).

Microsoft Defender customers can [turn on attack surface reduction rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to prevent common attack techniques used in infostealer infections. Attack surface reduction rules are sweeping settings that stop entire classes of threats including, infostealers, credential theft, and ransomware. The following bullet points offer more guidance on specific mitigation advice:

- [Turn on PUA protection in block mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/detect-block-potentially-unwanted-apps-microsoft-defender-antivirus?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc)
- [Block executable files from running unless they meet a prevalence, age, or trusted list criterion](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-executable-files-from-running-unless-they-meet-a-prevalence-age-or-trusted-list-criterion)
- [Block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-execution-of-potentially-obfuscated-scripts)

## Detections/Hunting Queries

### Microsoft Defender Antivirus
Microsoft Defender Antivirus detects threat components as the following malware:
 
- [Trojan:Win32/Vidar](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=Trojan:Win32/Vidar.A)
- Trojan:Win32/Etset!rfn

## References
[DeepSeek Lure Using CAPTCHAs To Spread Malware](https://www.zscaler.com/blogs/security-research/deepseek-lure-using-captchas-spread-malware). Zscaler (accessed 2025-02-25)
 
[Information Stealers](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/2296d491ea381b532b24f2575f9418d4b6723c17b8a1f507d20c2140a75d16d6). Microsoft (accessed 2025-02-25)

title: Auto-Color: An Emerging and Evasive Linux Backdoor
content:
#### Targeted Geolocations
- North America  
- Central Asia  
- East Asia  
- South Asia  
- Southeast Asia



#### Targeted Industries
- Government Agencies & Services  
- Education  
    - Higher Education



## Snapshot
Palo Alto Networks researchers discovered a new Linux malware named Auto-color, which employs advanced evasion techniques to avoid detection and grants threat actors full remote access to compromised machines.

## Description
This malware disguises itself by renaming its file to benign-sounding names like "door" or "egg," making it harder for security tools to identify. Once executed, Auto-color installs a malicious library, libcext.so.2, which hooks into core system libraries, allowing it to hide network activity and prevent removal. The malware also alters network activity data to conceal connections with its remote command-and-control (C2) servers, making it more difficult to detect its presence.

Auto-color's custom encryption protocol helps hide the configuration details for these C2 servers, which are dynamically configured based on the target system. The malware supports various functions through a specialized API, including reverse shell creation, file manipulation, and using the infected machine as a proxy. It can also modify global payload configurations remotely, enabling attackers to maintain control over compromised systems. Auto-color's persistence is enhanced by modifying the /etc/ld.preload file, ensuring its malicious library is loaded before other system libraries. While its exact method of delivery remains unclear, Auto-color has been primarily used to target universities and government offices in North America and Asia.

## Recommendations
Microsoft recommends the following mitigations to reduce the impact of this threat.
 
- Turn on [cloud-delivered protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/linux-preferences) in Microsoft Defender Antivirus or the equivalent for your antivirus product to cover rapidly evolving attacker tools and techniques. Cloud-based machine learning protections block a majority of new and unknown threats.
- Run [EDR in block mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/edr-in-block-mode?view=o365-worldwide?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) so that Microsoft Defender for Endpoint can block malicious artifacts, even when your non-Microsoft antivirus does not detect the threat or when Microsoft Defender Antivirus is running in passive mode. EDR in block mode works behind the scenes to remediate malicious artifacts that are detected post-breach.
- Allow [investigation and remediation](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/automated-investigations?view=o365-worldwide?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in full automated mode to allow Microsoft Defender for Endpoint to take immediate action on alerts to resolve breaches, significantly reducing alert volume.
- [Enable](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/enable-controlled-folders) controlled folder access.
- Ensure that [tamper protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/prevent-changes-to-security-settings-with-tamper-protection#how-do-i-configure-or-manage-tamper-protection) is enabled in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
- Enable [network protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/enable-network-protection) in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
- Follow the credential hardening recommendations in the [on-premises credential theft overview](https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/9382203e-5155-4b5e-af74-21562b1004d5/analystreport) to defend against common credential theft techniques like LSASS access.
- [Enable](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference#block-credential-stealing-from-the-windows-local-security-authority-subsystem) LSA protection.

## References
[Auto-Color: An Emerging and Evasive Linux Backdoor](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/new-linux-backdoor-auto-color/). Palo Alto Networks (accessed 2025-02-25)

title: Silent Killers: Unmasking a Large-Scale Legacy Driver Exploitation Campaign
content:
#### Targeted Geolocations
- China  
- Central Asia  
- East Asia  
- South Asia  
- Southeast Asia



## Snapshot
Check Point Research (CPR) has identified a sophisticated campaign exploiting a vulnerability in the legacy Truesight.sys driver, version 2.0.2, to bypass detection methods.

## Description
The campaign, linked with moderately high confidence to the threat actor SilverFox, primarily impacts victims in China and other parts of Asia. The attackers exploited a Windows driver signing loophole, using over 2,500 unique variants of the legacy Truesight.sys driver (version 2.0.2) to evade detection while maintaining valid digital signatures. By modifying certain PE file components, they generated unique hashes, allowing the driver to bypass security measures.

The infection chain consists of three stages, beginning with initial-stage malware disguised as legitimate applications and distributed via phishing websites and messaging apps. This malware acts as a downloader, leading to an EDR/AV killer module that terminates security processes using Truesight.sys and IOCTL 0x22E044 for arbitrary process termination. The final payload is a variant of Gh0st RAT, possibly HiddenGh0st, a stealthy remote access trojan used for surveillance and data theft. Attackers leveraged an existing proof-of-concept exploit but developed their own custom implementation to enhance evasion.

The campaign's infrastructure is hosted in a public cloud’s China region, where command-and-control (C2) servers operate. To maintain persistence, the malware employs DLL side-loading, in-memory payload decryption, and process injection techniques. Additionally, the attackers use VMProtect to obfuscate the malware, making analysis difficult, particularly due to the reliance on 32-bit code. The EDR/AV killer module specifically targets a hardcoded list of 192 security-related processes to disable endpoint defenses. According to Check Point Research, this operation demonstrates highly sophisticated evasion tactics, leveraging legacy vulnerabilities to deploy advanced remote access tools while maintaining long-term persistence.r than reported.

## Microsoft Analysis and Additional OSINT Context
In a Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) attack, also known as Living Off The Land Drivers (LOLDrivers), a threat actor drops a legitimate, signed driver containing an exploitable vulnerability onto a compromised system to exploit that vulnerability with a separate malicious tool. This technique differs from signed malicious drivers. While the signed driver in BYOVD is developed by a legitimate developer, a signed malicious driver is developed by a threat actor. 
 
While a variety of threat actors have used BYOVD in campaigns, this tactic is particularly popular among financially motivated threat actors. Threat actors and security researchers publish databases of exploitable drivers on the internet. These let threat actors identify and obtain vulnerable drivers that suit their needs in a specific campaign. These databases also help defenders locate drivers that should be removed from systems, or else carefully monitored for exploitation. Microsoft publishes a [vulnerable driver blocklist](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/application-security/application-control/windows-defender-application-control/design/microsoft-recommended-driver-block-rules), which Windows Security uses to stop vulnerable drivers from running on the system.
 
Depending on the specific driver exploited, a threat actor might accomplish one of several goals, including [defense evasion](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1211), and [privilege escalation](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068). Most commonly, threat actors use this technique to [turn off security software](https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/9ce0ac71-e104-4e59-9d46-2a8e2cac5a1d/analystreport).
 
To learn more about BYOVD attacks, read Microsoft's [technique profile](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/16be9ec5) on the topic. Microsoft Defender for Endpoint detects vulnerable drivers with the alert *Known vulnerable driver loaded*. Organizations can further limit the impact of BYOVD attacks with the attack surface reduction rule to [block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference?view=o365-worldwide#block-abuse-of-exploited-vulnerable-signed-drivers).

## Recommendations
Microsoft recommends the following mitigations to reduce the impact of this threat. Check the recommendations card for the deployment status of monitored mitigations.
 
- Ensure that the [Microsoft vulnerable driver blocklist](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/application-security/application-control/windows-defender-application-control/design/microsoft-recommended-driver-block-rules) and [Memory integrity](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/hardware-security/enable-virtualization-based-protection-of-code-integrity) (also known as hypervisor-protected code integrity or HVCI) are enabled for all devices. With Windows 11 2022 update, the vulnerable driver blocklist is enabled by default for all devices and can be turned on or off using the Windows Security app. Except on Windows Server 2016, the vulnerable driver blocklist is also enforced when either Memory integrity (HVCI), Smart App Control, or S mode is active. Users can opt in to HVCI using the Windows Security app, and HVCI is on by-default for most new Windows 11 devices.
- Alternatively, use Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) to [block vulnerable drivers](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/application-security/application-control/windows-defender-application-control/design/microsoft-recommended-driver-block-rules#blocking-vulnerable-drivers-using-wdac).
- Provide training to help end users identify risky executable files and avoid risky behavior, such as searching the internet for and installing third-party applications.
- Microsoft Defender XDR customers can turn on [attack surface reduction rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction)to prevent common attack techniques:
    - [Block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference?view#block-abuse-of-exploited-vulnerable-signed-drivers)
    - [Block executable files from running unless they meet a prevalence, age, or trusted list criterion](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference#block-executable-files-from-running-unless-they-meet-a-prevalence-age-or-trusted-list-criterion)
    - [Block all Office applications from creating child processes](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference?view#block-all-office-applications-from-creating-child-processes)

###

## Detections/Hunting Queries

### Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
Alerts with the following titles can indicate threat activity on your network:
 
- Known vulnerable driver loaded
- Driver with invalid certificate loaded

## References
[Silent Killers: Unmasking a Large-Scale Legacy Driver Exploitation Campaign](https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/large-scale-exploitation-of-legacy-driver/). Check Point Research (accessed 2025-02-25)

title: The GitVenom campaign: cryptocurrency theft using GitHub
content:
#### Targeted Geolocations
- Russia  
- Brazil  
- Türkiye



## Snapshot
Researchers at Kaspersky's SecureList have reported on the GitVenom campaign, a malicious operation targeting GitHub users through fake projects that contain embedded malware. Hundreds of repositories have been created, offering seemingly legitimate projects such as Instagram automation tools, Bitcoin wallet managers, and hacking tools for games like Valorant.

## Description
These repositories are designed to appear authentic, with detailed README.md files and inflated commit histories. The malicious code varies depending on the programming language used in the project, with Python projects containing long lines of code for decrypting and executing scripts, JavaScript projects having malicious functions invoked from the main file, and C, C++, and C# projects hiding malicious batch scripts in Visual Studio project files.

The payloads are designed to download and execute further malicious components from attacker-controlled repositories. These include a Node.js stealer that collects sensitive information and sends it to the attackers via Telegram, the open-source [AsyncRAT](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/e9216610feb409dfb620b28e510f2ae2582439dfc7c7e265815ff1a776016776) and Quasar backdoors, and a clipboard hijacker that replaces cryptocurrency wallet addresses in the clipboard with those controlled by the attackers. One such Bitcoin wallet amassed approximately 485,000 USD in November 2024. The campaign has been active for several years, with infection attempts observed worldwide, particularly in Russia, Brazil, and Turkey.

## Recommendations
While every situation is unique to the customer and their environment, the following recommendations are broadly applicable to help identify and mitigate cryptojacking attacks:  
 
- Implement MFA: Ensure comprehensive use of [MFA](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/authentication/tutorial-enable-azure-mfa), particularly for accounts with virtual machine contributor privileges. Discourage password reuse. A full list of cloud security recommendations can be found in [Security recommendations – a reference guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/defender-for-cloud/recommendations-reference?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc).
- Use risk-based sign-in behaviors and conditional access policies: Monitor high Azure Active Directory risk scores and correlate risky behavior with subsequent activity. Implement conditional access policies for multifactor reauthentication, device compliance, password updates, or blocking authentication.
- Detect login anomalies: Employ standard anomaly detection methods for identifying unusual login patterns, such as proxy usage, anomalous locations, and user agents. Utilize Microsoft 365 Defender for detecting suspicious activities performed by risky users.
- Monitor external Azure IP addresses: Authentication from non-tenant IP addresses should be considered anomalous. Use the [az vm list-ip-addresses](https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/vm?view=azure-cli-latest#az-vm-list-ip-addresses) command to identify allocated IP addresses within the tenant.
- Monitor quota increases: Watch for unexpected quota increases, especially across multiple regions or for rarely used resources, as they may indicate resource abuse attacks. Quota increase detections can be refined by focusing on commonly abused core types.

## References
[The GitVenom campaign: cryptocurrency theft using GitHub](https://securelist.com/gitvenom-campaign/115694/). SecureList by Kaspersky (accessed 2025-02-24)
 
 [AsyncRAT](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/e9216610feb409dfb620b28e510f2ae2582439dfc7c7e265815ff1a776016776). Microsoft (accessed 2025-02-24)

title: Target activity of UAC-0212 in relation to developers and suppliers of ICS solutions for the purpose of cyberattacks on critical infrastructure facilities of Ukraine
content:
## Snapshot
The Government Computer Emergency Response Team of Ukraine (CERT-UA) has uncovered a new wave of cyberattacks targeting Ukrainian logistics, industrial automation, and grain processing enterprises, with additional victims in Serbia and the Czech Republic. These attacks, linked to UAC-0212, a subcluster of UAC-0002 ([Seashell Blizzard](https://sip.security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/cf1e406a16835d56cf614430aea3962d7ed99f01ee3d9ee3048078288e5201bb)), indicate a strategic effort to compromise Ukraine’s critical infrastructure supply chain.

## Description
Between July 2024 and February 2025, attackers focused on logistics providers, grain equipment manufacturers, and automated process control systems (APCS) developers, all essential to Ukraine’s energy, water, and industrial sectors. The attacks involved prolonged social engineering, where adversaries, posing as customers, tricked victims into opening malicious PDF links that exploited CVE-2024-38213 to execute PowerShell scripts and deploy malware like SECONDBEST, EMPIREPAST, SPARK, and CROOKBAG. By January 2025, hackers had already infiltrated at least twenty-five ICS service providers, potentially affecting hundreds of critical enterprises.

CERT-UA warns that simple remediation, like antivirus scans or OS reinstalls, is insufficient, as attackers quickly move laterally within networks, gaining persistence on servers and critical systems. Organizations are urged to review threat indicators, examine potential compromises, and report suspicious activity to CERT-UA for forensic analysis and incident response.

## Microsoft Analysis and Additional OSINT Context
In February, Microsoft published a security blog highlight our research into a subgroup within the Russian state actor Seashell Blizzard and its multiyear initial access operation, tracked by Microsoft Threat Intelligence as the “BadPilot campaign”. This subgroup has conducted globally diverse compromises of Internet-facing infrastructure to enable Seashell Blizzard to persist on high-value targets and support tailored network operations. Read more here about [The BadPilot campaign: Seashell Blizzard subgroup conducts multiyear global access operation](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2025/02/12/the-badpilot-campaign-seashell-blizzard-subgroup-conducts-multiyear-global-access-operation/)

## Recommendations
Microsoft recommends the following mitigations to reduce the impact of this threat
 
**Strengthen operating environment configuration**
 
- Utilize a vulnerability management system, such as [Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-vulnerability-management/defender-vulnerability-management), to manage vulnerabilities, weaknesses, and remediation efforts across your environment's operating systems, software inventories, and [network devices](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/network-devices).
- Require [multifactor authentication (MFA)](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/security-and-compliance/set-up-multi-factor-authentication). While certain attacks such as AiTM phishing attempt to circumvent MFA, implementation of MFA remains an essential pillar in identity security and is highly effective at stopping a variety of threats.
    - Leverage [phishing-resistant authentication methods](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/concept-authentication-methods) such as FIDO Tokens, or [Microsoft Authenticator](https://www.microsoft.com/security/mobile-authenticator-app) with passkey. Avoid telephony-based MFA methods to avoid risks associated with SIM-jacking.
- Implement Entra ID [Conditional Access authentication strength](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/authentication/concept-authentication-strengths) to require phishing-resistant authentication for employees and external users for critical apps.
- Encourage users to use Microsoft Edge and other web browsers that support [Microsoft Defender SmartScreen](https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/microsoft-edge-security-smartscreen), which identifies and blocks malicious websites, including phishing sites, scam sites, and sites that host malware.
- Organizations can also use [Microsoft Defender External Attack Surface Management (EASM)](https://www.microsoft.com/security/business/cloud-security/microsoft-defender-external-attack-surface-management) , a tool that continuously discovers and maps digital attack surface to provide an external view of your online infrastructure. EASM leverages vulnerability and infrastructure data to generate Attack Surface Insights, reporting that highlights key risks to a given organization.
- Enable [Network Level Authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-server-2008-R2-and-2008/cc753488%28v=ws.11%29) for Remote Desktop Service connections.
- Enable [AppLocker](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/application-security/application-control/windows-defender-application-control/applocker/applocker-overview) to restrict specific software tools prohibited within the organization, such as reconnaissance, fingerprinting, and RMM tools, or grant access to only specific users.

**Strengthen Microsoft Defender for Endpoint configuration**

- Ensure that [tamper protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/prevent-changes-to-security-settings-with-tamper-protection#how-do-i-configure-or-manage-tamper-protection) is enabled in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
- Enable [network protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/enable-network-protection) in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
- Turn on [web protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/web-protection-overview).
- Run [endpoint detection and response (EDR) in block mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/edr-in-block-mode) so that Microsoft Defender for Endpoint can block malicious artifacts, even when your non-Microsoft antivirus does not detect the threat or when Microsoft Defender Antivirus is running in passive mode. EDR in block mode works behind the scenes to remediate malicious artifacts that are detected post-breach.
- Configure [investigation and remediation](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/automated-investigations) in full automated mode to let Microsoft Defender for Endpoint take immediate action on alerts to resolve breaches, significantly reducing alert volume.
- Microsoft Defender XDR customers can turn on the following [attack surface reduction rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction)to prevent common attack techniques used by threat actors.
    - [Block executable content from email client and webmail](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference#block-executable-content-from-email-client-and-webmail)
    - [Block executable files from running unless they meet a prevalence, age, or trusted list criterion](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference#block-executable-files-from-running-unless-they-meet-a-prevalence-age-or-trusted-list-criterion)
    - [Block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference#block-execution-of-potentially-obfuscated-scripts)
    - [Block JavaScript or VBScript from launching downloaded executable content](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference?block-javascript-or-vbscript-from-launching-downloaded-executable-content)
    - [Block process creations originating from PSExec and WMI commands](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference%22%20/l%20%22block-process-creations-originating-from-psexec-and-wmi-commands)

**Strengthen Microsoft Defender Antivirus configuration**

- Turn on [cloud-delivered protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/configure-block-at-first-sight-microsoft-defender-antivirus) in Microsoft Defender Antivirus, or the equivalent for your antivirus product, to cover rapidly evolving attacker tools and techniques. Cloud-based machine learning protections block a majority of new and unknown variants.
- Turn on Microsoft Defender Antivirus scanning of [downloaded files and attachments](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/configure-advanced-scan-types-microsoft-defender-antivirus?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc%22HYPERLINK%20%22https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/configure-advanced-scan-types-microsoft-defender-antivirus?view=o365-worldwide).

**Strengthen Microsoft Defender for Office 365 configuration**

- Turn on [zero-hour auto purge (ZAP)](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/zero-hour-auto-purge) in Microsoft Defender for Office 365 to quarantine sent mail in response to newly acquired threat intelligence and retroactively neutralize malicious phishing, spam, or malware messages that have already been delivered to mailboxes.

Run spear-phishing (credential harvest) simulations to train users against clicking URLs in unsolicited messages and disclosing credentials.

title: Patch Now: Check Point Research Explains Shadow Pad, NailaoLocker, and its Protection
content:
#### Targeted Geolocations
- Eastern Europe  
- Northern Europe  
- Southern Europe  
- Western Europe  
- North America  
- South America  
- Central America and the Caribbean  
- North Africa  
- Sub-Saharan Africa



#### Targeted Industries
- Critical Manufacturing



## Snapshot
A threat activity cluster has been exploiting the patched Check Point vulnerability, CVE-2024-24919, to deploy ShadowPad malware, and in some instances, this has led to the further deployment of NailaoLocker ransomware. The campaign, active from June 2024 to January 2025, predominantly targeted the manufacturing sector across Europe, Africa, and the Americas.

## Description
Attackers exploited the vulnerability to gain intial access, log into the VPN with valid accounts, and perform network scanning. They used used RDP or SMB to connect to Domain Controllers and executed legitimate programs to load malicious DLLs through DLL Sideloading. This technique installed [ShadowPad](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/shadowpad), which features advanced obfuscation and anti-debugging techniques and establishes remote access to systems.
 
In a subset of cases, NailaoLocker ransomware was also deployed.

## Microsoft Analysis and Additional OSINT Context
[CVE-2024-24919](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/CVE-2024-24919) is an information disclosure vulnerability that could allow unauthorized access to certain data on Check Point Security Gateways when connected to the internet and enabled with Check Point's Remote Access VPN or Mobile Access Software Blades. [GreyNoise](https://www.greynoise.io/blog/whats-going-on-with-checkpoint-cve-2024-24919) reported exploitation of the vulnerability in early April, while [WatchTowr Labs](https://labs.watchtowr.com/check-point-wrong-check-point-cve-2024-24919/) observed exploitation in late May. Check Point disclosed CVE-2024-24919 and release [security updates](https://support.checkpoint.com/results/sk/sk182336) for address the vulnerability. Multiple proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits have been published, making it critical to patch the vulnerability immediately.

## Recommendations
Apply these mitigations to reduce the impact of this threat. Check the recommendations card for the deployment status of monitored mitigations.
 
- Educate users about [preventing malware infections](https://www.microsoft.com/security/business/security-101/what-is-malware?ocid=magicti_ta_abbreviatedmktgpage"%20\t%20"_blank), such as ignoring or deleting unsolicited and unexpected emails or attachments sent through instant messaging applications or social networks as well as suspicious phone calls.
- Turn on [cloud-delivered protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/configure-block-at-first-sight-microsoft-defender-antivirus?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in Microsoft Defender Antivirus or the equivalent for your antivirus product to cover rapidly evolving attacker tools and techniques. Cloud-based machine learning protections block a huge majority of new and unknown variants.
- Turn on [tamper protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/prevent-changes-to-security-settings-with-tamper-protection?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) features to prevent attackers from stopping security services.
- Run [EDR in block mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/edr-in-block-mode?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) so that Microsoft Defender for Endpoint can block malicious artifacts, even when your non-Microsoft antivirus doesn’t detect the threat or when Microsoft Defender Antivirus is running in passive mode. EDR in block mode works behind the scenes to remediate malicious artifacts that are detected post-breach.
- Enable [network protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/enable-network-protection?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to prevent applications or users from accessing malicious domains and other malicious content on the internet.
- Enable [investigation and remediation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/automated-investigations?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in full automated mode to allow Microsoft Defender for Endpoint to take immediate action on alerts to resolve breaches, significantly reducing alert volume.
- Use [device discovery](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/device-discovery?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to increase your visibility into your network by finding unmanaged devices on your network and onboarding them to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
- Refer to [Microsoft’s human-operated ransomware overview](https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/05658b6c-dc62-496d-ad3c-c6a795a33c27/analystreport) for general hardening recommendations against ransomware attacks.

Microsoft Defender XDR customers can turn on [attack surface reduction rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to prevent common attack techniques used in ransomware attacks. Attack surface reduction rules are sweeping settings that are effective at stopping entire classes of threats:

- Ransom and lateral movement stage:
    - [Block executable files from running unless they meet a prevalence, age, or trusted list criterion](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-executable-files-from-running-unless-they-meet-a-prevalence-age-or-trusted-list-criterion)
    - [Use advanced protection against ransomware](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#use-advanced-protection-against-ransomware)
- Common techniques:
    - [Block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-execution-of-potentially-obfuscated-scripts)
    - [Block JavaScript or VBScript from launching downloaded executable content](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-javascript-or-vbscript-from-launching-downloaded-executable-content)

Check Point released [patches security updates](https://support.checkpoint.com/results/sk/sk182336) for this issue on May 28, 2024. Customers who have not applied the updates are urged to do so as soon as possible for their organization’s security. Check Point also recommended these additional security measures organizations should take:  

1. Disable the Remote Access VPN blade
2. Change the administrator passwords and use complex passwords
3. Restrict access through "Reach My Device"
4. Enable two-factor authentication for administrators (R81.10.10 and higher)
5. Enable two-factor authentication for Remote Access VPN users (R81.10.10 and higher)
6. Enable notifications for administrator access
7. Reinitialize internal Certificate Authority (CA)
8. Change the shared secret in the RADIUS Server settings
9. Change the shared secret in the TACACS+ Server settings
10. Change the password in the Active Directory server settings
11. Change the password in the Wireless settings
12. Change the password of the LDAP Account Unit
13. Reset password of local accounts connecting to Remote Access VPN with password-only authentication
14. Prevent local accounts from connecting to VPN with password-only authentication
15. Renew the server certificates for the Inbound HTTPS Inspection on the Security Gateway
16. Renew the certificate for the Outbound HTTPS Inspection on the Security Gateway
17. Reset Gaia OS passwords for all local users
18. Regenerate the SSH local user certificate on the Security Gateway in the following case:
    - Based on the [check-for-CVE-2024-24919.sh](https://support.checkpoint.com/results/download/133115) script results, your Security Gateway is vulnerable. For more information on running the check-for-CVE-2024-24919.sh script, Check Point’s instructions can be found labeled under [procedure to identify vulnerable Security Gateways.](https://support.checkpoint.com/results/sk/sk182336)
    - On the Security Gateway, the SSH is configured to allow all source IP addresses, including the internet (not recommended).
    - Authentication of SSH users is based on certificates.
    - You did not delete the user's private key from the Security Gateway (not recommended).
        - You can find the user's private keys in the `/home/<username>/.ssh` file.
        - Use the command in the Expert mode: `find /home/*/.ssh -print`
        - In the command output, you should see a file called `id_rsa` (this is the private SSH key).
        - For each of these keys, use the `ssh-keygen` command (in the Expert mode) to regenerate the SSH key for the relevant user.
19. Renew the certificate for the SSH Inspection
20. Update Azure high availability (HA) credentials

## Detections/Hunting Queries

### Microsoft Defender Antivirus
Microsoft Defender Antivirus detects threat components as the following malware:
 
- Trojan:Win32/Alevaul!rfn
- Trojan:Win64/DllHijack!rfn
- Program:Win32/Wacapew.C!ml
- [Trojan:Win64/DllHijack](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=Trojan:Win64/DllHijack!MSR)

[Preventative Hotfix for CVE-2024-24919 - Quantum Gateway Information Disclosure](https://support.checkpoint.com/results/sk/sk182336). Check Point (accessed 2025-02-25)
 
[CVE-2024-24919](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/CVE-2024-24919). Microsoft (accessed 2025-02-25)

[Check Point - Wrong Check Point (CVE-2024-24919)](https://labs.watchtowr.com/check-point-wrong-check-point-cve-2024-24919/). Wtchtowr (accessed 2025-02-25)

title: Angry Likho: Old beasts in a new forest
content:
#### Targeted Geolocations
- Russia  
- Belarus



#### Targeted Industries
- Government Agencies & Services



## Snapshot
Researchers at SecureList by Kaspersky have identified continued activity from the APT group Angry Likho, also known as Sticky Werewolf, with a new wave of attacks observed in January 2025.

## Description
Angry Likho primarily targets employees of large organizations, including government agencies and contractors, using spear-phishing emails containing malicious RAR archives. These archives typically include two LNK files and a bait document written in Russian, suggesting that the attackers are native Russian speakers. The group employs self-extracting archives (SFX) to deliver their malware, leveraging the Nullsoft Scriptable Install System to drop files into hidden directories.
 
A key implant used in their recent campaign is a malicious AutoIt script, which executes obfuscated commands to deploy additional payloads while evading detection. The attackers implement anti-analysis techniques, such as checking for security research environments and delaying execution to bypass automated detection tools. The final payload of their latest attacks is the Lumma stealer, a trojan capable of extracting credentials, cookies, cryptocurrency wallet data, and authentication information from compromised systems. Analysis of command servers linked to Angry Likho's malware revealed multiple domains used for data exfiltration and communication.
 
In January 2025, the group introduced a new technique, embedding malicious .NET payloads within Base64-encoded image files, a method they had previously used in earlier campaigns. This shift suggests an evolution in their approach while maintaining core attack strategies. The surge in activity observed in January, combined with the reuse of filenames and techniques, indicates that Angry Likho remains an active and persistent cyber threat. Most victims of this campaign are located in Russia and Belarus, and have impacted employees of government-related entities.

## Recommendations
Microsoft recommends the following mitigations to reduce the impact of this threat. 
 
- Educate users about [protecting personal and business information](https://www.microsoft.com/security/business/security-101/what-is-email-security) in social media, filtering unsolicited communication, identifying lure links in phishing emails, and reporting reconnaissance attempts and other suspicious activity.

- Invest in advanced anti-phishing solutions that monitor incoming emails and visited websites. [Microsoft Defender for Office 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-xdr/microsoft-365-security-center-mdo) brings together incident and alert management across email, devices, and identities, centralizing investigations for email-based threats.
- Encourage users to use Microsoft Edge and other web browsers that support [Microsoft Defender SmartScreen](https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/microsoft-edge-security-smartscreen), which identifies and blocks malicious websites, including phishing sites, scam sites, and sites that host malware.
- Implement [Conditional Access authentication strength](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/concept-authentication-strengths) to require phishing-resistant authentication for employees and external users for critical apps.
- Turn on [cloud-delivered protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/enable-cloud-protection-microsoft-defender-antivirus) in Microsoft Defender Antivirus or the equivalent for your antivirus product to cover rapidly evolving attacker tools and techniques. Cloud-based machine learning protections block a huge majority of new and unknown variants.
- Enable [network protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/enable-network-protection) to prevent applications or users from accessing malicious domains and other malicious content on the internet.
- Turn on [tamper protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/prevent-changes-to-security-settings-with-tamper-protection) features to prevent attackers from stopping security services.
- Enable [investigation and remediation](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/automated-investigations) in full automated mode to allow Defender for Endpoint to take immediate action on alerts to resolve breaches, significantly reducing alert volume.
- Run [endpoint detection and response (EDR) in block mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/edr-in-block-mode), so that Defender for Endpoint can block malicious artifacts, even when your non-Microsoft antivirus doesn’t detect the threat or when Microsoft Defender Antivirus is running in passive mode. EDR in block mode works behind the scenes to remediate malicious artifacts detected post-breach.

Microsoft Defender XDR customers can turn on [attack surface reduction rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction) to prevent common attack techniques:

- [Block executable files from running unless they meet a prevalence, age, or trusted list criterion](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference#block-executable-files-from-running-unless-they-meet-a-prevalence-age-or-trusted-list-criterion)

## Detections/Hunting Queries

title: DPRK DriverEasy & ChromeUpdate Deep Dive
content:
## Snapshot
Kandji researchers investigated "DriverEasy," a malicious application disguised as a Google Chrome update to steal user credentials.

## Description
DriverEasy exploits Dropbox’s API to exfiltrate sensitive data, including passwords. Developed in Swift and Objective-C, it deceives users with fake prompts to capture system passwords, which are uploaded to Dropbox as "password.txt" via OAuth 2.0 authentication. The malware also queries the victim’s public IP and prepares predefined strings for transmission. Kandji reports that the malware is part of North Korea's cyber-espionage campaign, "[Contagious Interview](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/9ce29d67)." It shares identical Dropbox API credentials with applications used in previously documented North Korean threat actor campaigns, "ChromeUpdate" and "CameraAccess."

## Recommendations
Apply these mitigations to reduce the impact of this threat. Check the recommendations card for the deployment status of monitored mitigations.

- Turn on [cloud-delivered protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/configure-block-at-first-sight-microsoft-defender-antivirus?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc)  in Microsoft Defender Antivirus or the equivalent for your antivirus product to cover rapidly evolving attacker tools and techniques. Cloud-based machine learning protections block a huge majority of new and unknown variants.
- Turn on [tamper protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/prevent-changes-to-security-settings-with-tamper-protection?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc)  features to prevent attackers from stopping security services.
- Run [endpoint detection and response (EDR) in block mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/edr-in-block-mode?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc), so that Defender for Endpoint can block malicious artifacts, even when your non-Microsoft antivirus doesn’t detect the threat or when Microsoft Defender Antivirus is running in passive mode. EDR in block mode works behind the scenes to remediate malicious artifacts detected post-breach.
- Enable [investigation and remediation](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/automated-investigations?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc)  in full automated mode to allow Defender for Endpoint to take immediate action on alerts to resolve breaches, significantly reducing alert volume.
- Microsoft Defender customers can turn on [attack surface reduction rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc)  to prevent common attack techniques. Attack surface reduction rules are sweeping settings that are effective at stopping entire classes of threats.
- Implement multifactor authentication (MFA) to mitigate credential theft. Compliment MFA with the following solutions and best practices to protect organizations:  

    - Activate conditional access policies. [Conditional access](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/conditional-access/overview?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) policies are evaluated and enforced every time an attacker attempts to use a stolen session cookie. Conditional access policies evaluate sign-in requests using additional identity-driven signals like user or group membership, IP location information, and device status, among others, and are enforced for suspicious sign-ins. Organizations can protect themselves from attacks that leverage stolen credentials by enabling policies such as compliant devices or trusted IP address requirements.
    - Configure [continuous access evaluation](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/conditional-access/concept-continuous-access-evaluation?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in your tenant.
    - Block phishing websites and other malicious URLs and domains in the browser through [Microsoft Defender SmartScreen](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/virus-and-threat-protection/microsoft-defender-smartscreen/), as well as the detection of suspicious and malicious behavior on endpoints.

## References

title: Weathering the storm: In the midst of a Typhoon
content:
#### Targeted Geolocations
- United States



#### Targeted Industries
- Information Technology  
    - Internet-based Content, Information & Communication



## Snapshot
Cisco Talos has been tracking a sophisticated threat actor known as [Salt Typhoon](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/97d973d15f12895b3f1627cc441d5810903223c6c607da5500d370cc8b0c1632?tab=tradeCraft&), responsible for a series of intrusions targeting major US telecommunications companies.

## Description
The threat actor primarily gains access to core networking infrastructure using valid, stolen credentials and maintains long-term persistence to victim environments. While there is evidence that Salt Typhoon exploited a Cisco vulnerability ([CVE-2018-0171](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/cves/CVE-2018-0171/)) in one instance, Cisco has not confirmed reports from other security vendors suggesting the abuse of three other known Cisco vulnerabilities, [CVE-2023-20198](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/CVE-2023-20198), [CVE-2023-20273](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/cves/CVE-2023-20273/), and [CVE-2024-20399](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/cves/CVE-2024-20399/).
 
The actor employs living-off-the-land (LOTL) techniques and has been observed capturing SNMP, TACACS, and RADIUS traffic to harvest additional credentials. Once inside a network, they exfiltrate device configurations, including weakly encrypted credentials and SNMP community strings, often using TFTP and FTP. 

According to Cisco, Salt Typhoon frequently pivots through compromised infrastructure, moving between trusted network devices to evade detection. In several cases, the threat actor used a compromised telecom device as a hop point to access targets in other telecom organizations. Salt Typhoon's pivoting spans multiple vendors' equipment, further complicating detection and mitigation efforts.

In its campaign, Salt Typhoon leveraged JumbledPath, a custom-built utility written in GO, to execute packet capture on remote Cisco devices via an actor-defined jump host. The tool encrypted and compressed the captured data while also clearing logs to evade detection. By creating a chain of connections, JumbledPath obscured the origin and destination of the data, enabling movement through otherwise unreachable infrastructure. Compiled as an ELF binary for x86-64 architecture, it is compatible with various Linux-based network devices.

## Microsoft Analysis and Additional OSINT Context
The threat actor that Microsoft tracks as [Salt Typhoon](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/97d973d15f12895b3f1627cc441d5810903223c6c607da5500d370cc8b0c1632?tab=tradeCraft&) is a nation-state threat actor based out of China. Salt Typhoon is known to primarily target communications infrastructure, military, and law enforcement organizations in North America, Oceania, South America, and Southeast Asia. Salt Typhoon focuses on espionage and data theft, with a particular focus on capturing network traffic and modifying network appliances. A key objective of Salt Typhoon is to maintain long-term persistence to compromised environments, primarily on compromised routing devices in sensitive network segments.

Salt Typhoon frequently gains initial access through publicly exposed devices, including those manufactured by Cisco, Fortinet, Palo Alto, and Ivanti. The threat actor is not known to exploit 0-day vulnerabilities. Instead, Salt Typhoon appears to leverage recently disclosed vulnerabilities.  While it’s likely that the threat actor will change which vulnerabilities it exposes over time, Salt Typhoon's most commonly exploited vulnerabilities include: 
 
- [CVE-2024-55591](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-55591): An Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel vulnerability CWE-288 affecting FortiOS version 7.0.0 through 7.0.16 and FortiProxy version 7.0.0 through 7.0.19 and 7.2.0 through 7.2.12.
- [CVE-2023-20198](https://blog.talosintelligence.com/active-exploitation-of-cisco-ios-xe-software/): A vulnerability in the web UI feature in Cisco IOS XE software used to gain initial access and issue a level 15 command to create a local user and password combination.
- [CVE-2023-20273](https://blog.talosintelligence.com/active-exploitation-of-cisco-ios-xe-software/): A vulnerability in the web UI feature of Cisco IOS XE software that could allow an authenticated, remote attacker to inject commands with root privileges.
- [CVE-2023-27997](https://www.fortinet.com/blog/psirt-blogs/analysis-of-cve-2023-27997-and-clarifications-on-volt-typhoon-campaign): A heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in FortiOS.
- [CVE-2022-42475](https://www.fortinet.com/blog/psirt-blogs/analysis-of-fg-ir-22-398-fortios-heap-based-buffer-overflow-in-sslvpnd): A heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in FortiOS SSL-VPN.

## Recommendations
Microsoft recommends the following mitigations to reduce the impact of this threat. Check the recommendations card for the deployment status of monitored mitigations.  

- Keep public-facing servers up to date to defend against malicious activity. As prime targets for threat actors, public-facing servers need additional monitoring and security. User input validation, file integrity monitoring, behavioral monitoring, and web application firewalls can all help to better secure these servers.
- Utilize a vulnerability management system, such as [Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-vulnerability-management/defender-vulnerability-management?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc), to manage vulnerabilities, weaknesses, and remediation efforts across your environment's operating systems, software inventories, and [network devices](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/network-devices?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc).
- Turn on [cloud-delivered protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/enable-cloud-protection-microsoft-defender-antivirus?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in Microsoft Defender Antivirus or the equivalent for your antivirus product to cover rapidly evolving attacker tools and techniques.
- Follow [best practices](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/security/fundamentals/network-best-practices?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) for enhancing network security for cloud computing environments.
- Enable [real-time protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/configure-real-time-protection-microsoft-defender-antivirus?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in Microsoft Defender Antivirus or the equivalent for your antivirus product.
- Utilize Microsoft Purview Information Protection or an equivalent information protection solution to [discover, classify, and protect](https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/information-protection?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) sensitive information across devices and applications.
- [Detect and block](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/detect-block-potentially-unwanted-apps-microsoft-defender-antivirus?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) potentially unwanted applications through Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
- [Run endpoint detection and response (EDR) in block mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/edr-in-block-mode?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) so that Microsoft Defender for Endpoint can block malicious artifacts, even when your non-Microsoft antivirus does not detect the threat, or when Microsoft Defender Antivirus is running in passive mode. EDR in block mode works behind the scenes to remediate malicious artifacts that are detected post-compromise.
- Turn on [attack surface reduction rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc)to prevent common attack techniques: 
    - [Block executable files from running unless they meet a prevalence, age, or trusted list criterion](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-executable-files-from-running-unless-they-meet-a-prevalence-age-or-trusted-list-criterion)
    - [Block credential stealing from the Windows local security authority subsystem (lsass.exe)](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-credential-stealing-from-the-windows-local-security-authority-subsystem)
    - [Block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-execution-of-potentially-obfuscated-scripts)
- Implement [anomaly detection](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-cloud-apps/anomaly-detection-policy?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) policies in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps.
- Enable protections in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint to safeguard against malicious sites and internet-based threats.
    - [Network protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/network-protection?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc)
    - [Web protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/web-protection-overview?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc)
- Enable [tamper protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/prevent-changes-to-security-settings-with-tamper-protection?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) within Microsoft Defender for Endpoint to prevent threat actors from disabling or changing security features, such as virus and threat protection.

## References

title: Stately Taurus Activity in Southeast Asia Links to Bookworm Malware
content:
#### Targeted Geolocations
- Myanmar  
- Southeast Asia



## Snapshot
Unit 42 researchers uncovered new connections between Stately Taurus and the Bookworm malware while investigating attacks on organizations linked to Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) countries.

## Description
Researchers identified overlapping infrastructure and activity, including a January 2024 post detailing attacks in Myanmar. Stately Taurus has a history of using DLL sideloading to execute PubLoad malware, a malware family unique to this group.
 
Before this analysis, no threat actor had been directly linked to Bookworm, but the evidence now suggests Stately Taurus has been using it for nearly a decade. The PubLoad malware communicates with its command and control (C2) server using URLs designed to mimic legitimate Microsoft Windows Update requests. Unit 42 researchers also found older payloads that shared URL patterns with Stately Taurus infrastructure, reinforcing the connection.
 
The malware’s unique shellcode-loading technique, adapted from publicly available source code, uses UUID strings and legitimate API callbacks to execute its payload. Bookworm samples from 2021 and 2022 show only minor changes from the 2015 versions, with updates to module naming conventions and a shift to embedding shellcode within UUID parameters.
 
A surprising overlap emerged with the ToneShell backdoor, as both malware families shared compile times, debug paths, and C2 infrastructure, further linking them to Stately Taurus. The adaptability of Bookworm, with its modular architecture and flexible shellcode packaging, makes it likely Stately Taurus will continue to leverage the malware in future operations.

## Recommendations
Microsoft recommends the following mitigations to reduce the impact of this threat.
 
- Turn on [cloud-delivered protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/linux-preferences) in Microsoft Defender Antivirus or the equivalent for your antivirus product to cover rapidly evolving attacker tools and techniques. Cloud-based machine learning protections block a majority of new and unknown threats.
- Run [EDR in block mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/edr-in-block-mode?view=o365-worldwide?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) so that Microsoft Defender for Endpoint can block malicious artifacts, even when your non-Microsoft antivirus does not detect the threat or when Microsoft Defender Antivirus is running in passive mode. EDR in block mode works behind the scenes to remediate malicious artifacts that are detected post-breach.
- Allow [investigation and remediation](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/automated-investigations?view=o365-worldwide?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in full automated mode to allow Microsoft Defender for Endpoint to take immediate action on alerts to resolve breaches, significantly reducing alert volume.
- [Enable](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/enable-controlled-folders) controlled folder access.
- Ensure that [tamper protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/prevent-changes-to-security-settings-with-tamper-protection#how-do-i-configure-or-manage-tamper-protection) is enabled in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
- Enable [network protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/enable-network-protection) in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
- Follow the credential hardening recommendations in the [on-premises credential theft overview](https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/9382203e-5155-4b5e-af74-21562b1004d5/analystreport) to defend against common credential theft techniques like LSASS access.
- [Enable](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference#block-credential-stealing-from-the-windows-local-security-authority-subsystem) LSA protection.

## Detections/Hunting Queries

### Microsoft Defender Antivirus
Microsoft Defender Antivirus detects threat components as the following malware:
 
- [Trojan:Win32/Wacatac](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=Trojan:Win32/Wacatac.B!ml)
- [Program:Win32/Wacapew](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=Program:Win32/Wacapew.C!ml)
- [PWS:Win32/Fareit](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=PWS:Win32/Fareit!ml)
- [TrojanDownloader:Win32/Reconyc](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=TrojanDownloader:Win32/Reconyc)

title: Darcula PhaaS can now auto-generate phishing kits for any brand
content:
## Snapshot
Netcraft researchers identified the Darcula phishing-as-a-service (PhaaS) platform's upcoming release, Darcula Suite, which features a DIY phishing kit generator. Cybercriminals are already migrating to it ahead of the launch.

## Description
Darcula Suite lets users generate phishing kits for any brand by entering a URL, which the platform clones using the Puppeteer tool. Darcula Suite also offers a user-friendly admin dashboard, IP and bot filtering, campaign performance tracking, automated credit card theft, and digital wallet loading. Emerging last year, the platform has been linked to 20,000 domains spoofing well-known brands to steal credentials worldwide. The new version simplifies phishing campaign creation and management with anti-detection features, real-time credential theft logs, and Telegram notifications for stolen information. It also provides a tool to convert stolen credit card data into virtual card images for digital payment apps. The beta's popularity is evident from a significant increase in its container image pull count.

Over the past 10 months, Netcraft has detected and blocked nearly 100,000 Darcula-related domains and IP addresses.

## Microsoft Analysis and Additional OSINT Context
[In July 2023](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/darcula-%E8%BE%BE%E5%B0%94%E5%BA%93%E6%8B%89-oshri-kalfon/), security researcher Oshri Kalfon first documented Darcula as a Chinese smishing software. [In March 2024](https://www.netcraft.com/blog/darcula-smishing-attacks-target-usps-and-global-postal-services/), Netcraft reported that the Darcula PhaaS, developed by a Telegram user of the same name, offered easy deployment of phishing sites with hundreds of templates targeting global brands. Built with JavaScript, React, and Docker, Darcula primarily targeted postal services, financial institutions, and government agencies, distributing phishing links via iMessage and RCS to bypass SMS firewalls. [Netcraft reports](https://www.netcraft.com/blog/darcula-v3-phishing-kits-targeting-any-brand/) the latest version, Darcula Suite (darcula 3.0), which maintains a signature cat-themed branding, is expected to launch this month.

## Recommendations
Implement multifactor authentication (MFA) to mitigate credential theft from phishing attacks. MFA can be complemented with the following solutions and best practices to protect organizations:  

- Activate conditional access policies. [Conditional access](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/conditional-access/overview?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) policies are evaluated and enforced every time an attacker attempts to use a stolen session cookie. Conditional access policies evaluate sign-in requests using additional identity-driven signals like user or group membership, IP location information, and device status, among others, and are enforced for suspicious sign-ins. Organizations can protect themselves from attacks that leverage stolen credentials by enabling policies such as compliant devices or trusted IP address requirements.
- Configure [continuous access evaluation](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/conditional-access/concept-continuous-access-evaluation?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in your tenant.
- Invest in advanced anti-phishing solutions that monitor incoming emails and visited websites. [Microsoft Defender for Office](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender/microsoft-365-security-center-mdo?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) 365 brings together incident and alert management across email, devices, and identities, centralizing investigations for threats in email. Organizations can also leverage web browsers that automatically [identify and block malicious websites](https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/microsoft-edge-security-smartscreen?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc). To build resilience against phishing attacks in general, organizations can use [anti-phishing policies](https://docs.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/set-up-anti-phishing-policies?view=o365-worldwide) to enable mailbox intelligence settings, as well as configure impersonation protection settings for specific messages and sender domains. Enabling [SafeLinks](https://docs.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/safe-links?view=o365-worldwide) ensures real-time protection by scanning at time of delivery and at time of click.
- Continuously monitor for suspicious or anomalous activities, and search for sign-in attempts with suspicious characteristics (for example location, internet service provider \[ISP\], user agent, and use of anonymizer services). Activity can be identified and investigated with [Microsoft Defender for Identity](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender/microsoft-365-security-center-mdi?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc), which contributes identity-focused information into incidents and alerts, providing key context and correlating alerts from other products within Microsoft 365 Defender. This ensures all alerts are available in one place, and the scope of a breach can be determined faster than before.

Defenders can also complement MFA with the following solutions and best practices to further protect their organizations from such attacks.  

- Use [security defaults](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/fundamentals/concept-fundamentals-security-defaults?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) as a baseline set of policies to improve identity security posture.
- Block phishing websites and other malicious URLs and domains in the browser through [Microsoft Defender SmartScreen](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/virus-and-threat-protection/microsoft-defender-smartscreen/), as well as the detection of suspicious and malicious behavior on endpoints.

## References
[Darcula PhaaS can now auto-generate phishing kits for any brand](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/darcula-phaas-can-now-auto-generate-phishing-kits-for-any-brand/). BleepingComputer (accessed 2025-02-20)
 
[The Bleeding Edge of Phishing: darcula-suite 3.0 Enables DIY Phishing of Any Brand](https://www.netcraft.com/blog/darcula-v3-phishing-kits-targeting-any-brand/). Netcraft (accessed 2025-02-20)
 
[Darcula - 达尔库拉](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/darcula-%E8%BE%BE%E5%B0%94%E5%BA%93%E6%8B%89-oshri-kalfon/). LinkedIn Pulse (accessed 2025-02-20)
 
[Out of the shadows – ’darcula’ iMessage and RCS smishing attacks target USPS and global postal services](https://www.netcraft.com/blog/darcula-smishing-attacks-target-usps-and-global-postal-services/). Netcraft (accessed 2025-02-20)
