title: SPAWNCHIMERA Malware: The Chimera Spawning from Ivanti Connect Secure Vulnerability
content:
## Snapshot
Researchers at the Japan Computer Emergency Response Team Coordination Center reported that the SPAWNCHIMERA malware, an evolution of the SPAWN malware family, exploited the CVE-2025-0282 vulnerability in Ivanti Connect Secure.

## Description
This vulnerability has been actively exploited in Japan since late December 2024, before Ivanti issued an advisory in January 2025. SPAWNCHIMERA incorporates the functionalities of SPAWNANT, SPAWNMOLE, and SPAWNSNAIL, without significant changes to its installation or process injection methods.
 
However, SPAWNCHIMERA has undergone several key updates. Notably, it now uses UNIX domain sockets for inter-process communication, making detection more difficult. It also includes a function to fix the CVE-2025-0282 vulnerability by hooking the `strncpy` function to limit the copy size, preventing other attackers from exploiting the same flaw. Additionally, the malware has introduced new decoding functions and removed debug messages to reduce traces and complicate analysis. Its SSH server functionality now uses an encoded private key, decoded through an XOR-based function, instead of relying on hardcoded plaintext. Furthermore, SPAWNCHIMERA identifies malicious traffic through a new decode function, replacing the previous hard-coded value. Given these sophisticated evolutions, SPAWNCHIMERA is expected to remain a persistent threat.

## Microsoft Analysis and Additional OSINT Context
Mandiant first [reported](https://sip.security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/7ab7c6bf?tid=72f988bf-86f1-41af-91ab-2d7cd011db47&view=description) malware on January 8, 2025, after discovering a zero-day exploit of CVE-2025-0282. Ivanti later issued a security advisory addressing [CVE-2025-0282](https://sip.security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/CVE-2025-0282), a buffer overflow vulnerability affecting its Connect Secure, Policy Secure, and ZTA Gateway products. This flaw allows threat actors to exploit improperly managed memory within the software, enabling unauthenticated remote code execution.
 
According to Mandiant, attackers deployed a suite of custom malware, including SPAWNANT, SPAWNMOLE, SPAWNSNAIL, SPAWNSLOTH, DRYHOOK, and PHASEJAM. SPAWNANT ensured persistence by hijacking the upgrade process and migrating malicious components to the new partition during system updates. SPAWNMOLE, a tunneler, established communication channels, while SPAWNSNAIL functioned as an SSH backdoor.
 
On January 16, 2025, Unit 42 [reported](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/67fc63fc) similar findings, confirming the exploitation of CVE-2025-0282 using SPAWNMOLE, SPAWNSNAIL, and SPAWNSLOTH.

## Recommendations
Ivanti released patches for the Ivanti Connect Secure vulnerability on January 8, 2025. Ivanti will also be releasing patches for the Policy Secure and ZTA Gateways vulnerabilities on January 21, 2025. Customers who use vulnerable Ivanti products are urged to patch as soon as possible for their organization’s security. Customers are also urged to reference the Ivanti security advisory for additional recommendations related to Ivanti’s Connect Secure vulnerability.  
   
Note that applying the patch does not remediate any exploitation or post-exploitation activity that might have occurred, and additional investigation might be warranted.  
   
Microsoft recommends the following mitigations to reduce the impact of this threat. Check the recommendations card for the deployment status of monitored mitigations to help investigate successful exploitation.
 
- Look for newly created users on devices impacted by the vulnerability and investigate virtual private network (VPN) logs for evidence of VPN configuration modifications or sign-in activity during the possible window of compromise of unpatched devices. Applying the security patch does not remediate post-compromise activity by a threat actor with privileged access.
    - In particular, [Volexity researchers have outlined several characteristics](https://www.volexity.com/blog/2024/01/10/active-exploitation-of-two-zero-day-vulnerabilities-in-ivanti-connect-secure-vpn/) of identified zero-day vulnerability exploitation, including lateral movement over Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP), Server Message Block (SMB), and Secure Shell (SSH), outbound connections using curl, reverse SOCKS proxy and SSH tunnel connections, and more suspicious activity.
- Turn on [cloud-delivered protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/enable-cloud-protection-microsoft-defender-antivirus) in Microsoft Defender Antivirus or the equivalent for your antivirus product to cover rapidly evolving attack tools and techniques. Cloud-based machine learning protections block a large majority of new and unknown variants.
- Run [endpoint detection and response (EDR) in block mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/edr-in-block-mode) so that Microsoft Defender for Endpoint can block malicious artifacts, even when your non-Microsoft antivirus doesn’t detect the threat or when Microsoft Defender Antivirus is running in passive mode. EDR in block mode works behind the scenes to remediate malicious artifacts that are detected post-breach.
- Enable [investigation and remediation](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/automated-investigations) in full automated mode to allow Microsoft Defender for Endpoint to take immediate action on alerts to resolve breaches, significantly reducing alert volume.
- Turn on [tamper protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/prevent-changes-to-security-settings-with-tamper-protection?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) features to prevent threat actors from stopping security services.
- Enable [network protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/enable-network-protection?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to prevent applications or users from accessing malicious domains and other malicious content on the internet..
- Use [device discovery](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/device-discovery?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to increase your visibility into your network by finding unmanaged devices on your network and onboarding them to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.

Microsoft Defender customers can turn on the following attack surface reduction rule to prevent common attack techniques:

- [Block executable files from running unless they meet a prevalence, age, or trusted list criterion](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference)
- You can assess how an attack surface reduction rule might impact your network by opening the [security recommendation](https://security.microsoft.com/security-recommendations) for that rule in threat and vulnerability management. In the recommendation details pane, check the user impact to determine what percentage of your devices can accept a new policy enabling the rule in blocking mode without adverse impact to user productivity.

Customers are strongly urged to keep all public-facing devices updated and to quickly implement patches when made available. Microsoft consistently observes Chinese nation-state threat actors target public facing devices across multiple vendors and products.

## References
[SPAWNCHIMERA Malware: The Chimera Spawning from Ivanti Connect Secure Vulnerability](https://blogs.jpcert.or.jp/en/2025/02/spawnchimera.html) JPCERT (accessed 2025-02-21)
 
[CVE-2025-0282 - Ivanti Connect Secure, Policy Secure, and ZTA Gateway](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/CVE-2025-0282) Microsoft (accessed 2025-02-21)
 
[Threat Brief: CVE-2025-0282 and CVE-2025-0283](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/67fc63fc). Microsoft (accessed 2025-02-21)
 
[Ivanti Connect Secure VPN Targeted in New Zero-Day Exploitation](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/7ab7c6bf). Microsoft (accessed 2025-02-21)

title: Backdoored Executables for Signal, Line, and Gmail Target Chinese-Speaking Users
content:
## Snapshot
Researchers at Hunt.io discovered a malicious campaign targeting Chinese-speaking users with malware-infected installers for popular applications such as Signal, Line, and Gmail. The attackers have been distributing these compromised applications through fake download pages hosted on unrelated domains, using sophisticated techniques to evade detection.

## Description
The attack likely relies on manipulating search engine results to direct users to fraudulent pages, which are hosted on Alibaba servers in Hong Kong, for software including Signal, Line, Gmail, and Google Translate. Unlike traditional phishing tactics, these domains do not attempt to mimic official software URLs. Each site delivers a ZIP file containing a malicious executable file. For example, the Signal spoofed site "z1.xiaowu\[.\]pw" provides a ZIP file named "Sriguoe-i4.zip," which contains a Windows executable disguised as a Signal installer. 

The malware, once executed, initiates a multi-step process that includes file extraction, process injection, and system modification, notably using PowerShell commands to disable Windows Defender by excluding the C: drive from scanning. Once the malware is executed from the user's desktop, it drops temporary files in the AppData directory, injects malicious processes into deeply nested paths, and establishes outbound connections to command-and-control (C2) servers.

## Microsoft Analysis and Additional OSINT Context
The use of software downloads as a lure remains a prevalent and highly effective cyber threat, exploiting user trust in well-known brands to facilitate malware infections. For example, in January, [researchers at Sekoia IO](https://sip.security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/1618082d) uncovered nearly 1,000 fraudulent websites impersonating Reddit and WeTransfer to deliver Lumma Stealer malware, leveraging a fake discussion thread and a deceptive WeTransfer link to manipulate victims. And in December, [Rapid7 Labs identified](https://sip.security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/b24308b0) the CleverSoar malware, which masquerades as gaming and software installers to specifically target Chinese and Vietnamese-speaking users, deploying advanced tools for data theft and system compromise. These incidents illustrate how adversaries systematically abuse the trust users place in established software brands, using sophisticated deception techniques to bypass skepticism and traditional security measures.

## Recommendations
Microsoft recommends the following mitigations to reduce the impact of infostealer threats.
 
- Check your Office 365 email filtering settings to ensure you block spoofed emails, spam, and emails with malware. Use [Microsoft Defender for Office 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/defender-for-office-365) for enhanced phishing protection and coverage against new threats and polymorphic variants. Configure Microsoft Defender for Office 365 to [recheck links on click](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/safe-links-about) and [delete sent mail](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/zero-hour-auto-purge) in response to newly acquired threat intelligence. Turn on [safe attachments policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/safe-attachments-policies-configure) to check attachments to inbound email.
- Encourage users to use Microsoft Edge and other web browsers that support [SmartScreen](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/web-protection-overview), which identifies and blocks malicious websites, including phishing sites, scam sites, and sites that host malware.
- Turn on [cloud-delivered protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/configure-block-at-first-sight-microsoft-defender-antivirus) in Microsoft Defender Antivirus, or the equivalent for your antivirus product, to cover rapidly evolving attacker tools and techniques. Cloud-based machine learning protections block a majority of new and unknown variants.
- Enforce MFA on all accounts, remove users excluded from MFA, and strictly [require MFA](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/identity-protection/howto-identity-protection-configure-mfa-policy) from all devices, in all locations, at all times.
- Enable passwordless authentication methods (for example, Windows Hello, FIDO keys, or Microsoft Authenticator) for accounts that support passwordless. For accounts that still require passwords, use authenticator apps like Microsoft Authenticator for MFA. [Refer to this article](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/authentication/concept-authentication-methods) for the different authentication methods and features.
- For MFA that uses authenticator apps, ensure that the app requires a code to be typed in where possible, as many intrusions where MFA was enabled still succeeded due to users clicking “Yes” on the prompt on their phones even when they were not at their [devices](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/authentication/how-to-mfa-number-match). Refer to [this article](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/authentication/concept-authentication-methods) for an example.
- Remind employees that enterprise or workplace credentials should not be stored in browsers or password vaults secured with personal credentials. Organizations can turn off password syncing in browser on managed devices using [Group Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/microsoft-edge-enterprise-sync#sync-group-policies).

Microsoft Defender customers can [turn on attack surface reduction rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction) to prevent common attack techniques used in infostealer infections. Attack surface reduction rules are sweeping settings that stop entire classes of threats including, infostealers, credential theft, and ransomware. The following bullet points offer more guidance on specific mitigation advice:

- [Turn on PUA protection in block mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/detect-block-potentially-unwanted-apps-microsoft-defender-antivirus)
- [Block executable files from running unless they meet a prevalence, age, or trusted list criterion](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference)
- [Block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference)

## Detections/Hunting Queries

### Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
The following alerts might indicate threat activity associated with this threat. These alerts, however, can be triggered by unrelated threat activity and are not monitored in the status cards provided with this report.  
 
- Information stealing malware activity

title: Signals of Trouble: Multiple Russia-Aligned Threat Actors Actively Targeting Signal Messenger
content:
## Snapshot
Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) has detected increased efforts by Russia-aligned threat actors, including APT44, UNC5792, UNC4221, and Belarus-linked UNC1151, to compromise Signal Messenger accounts, particularly targeting individuals of interest to Russian intelligence services.

## Description
Multiple Russia-aligned threat actors are exploiting Signal's "linked devices" feature by crafting malicious QR codes that link the victim's account to an actor-controlled Signal instance, allowing real-time eavesdropping. APT44, tracked by Microsoft as [Seashell Blizzard](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/cf1e406a16835d56cf614430aea3962d7ed99f01ee3d9ee3048078288e5201bb), has been using this technique to link captured devices on the battlefield to their infrastructure, while UNC5792 (which partially overlaps with CERT-UA's [UAC-0195](https://cert.gov.ua/article/6278735)) and UNC4221 (tracked by CERT-UA as [UAC-0185](https://cert.gov.ua/article/6281632)) have been conducting phishing campaigns. UNC4221 is also deploying a JavaScript payload called PINPOINT to collect user information and geolocation data. 

In addition to these phishing efforts, there have been instances of direct exfiltration of Signal messages. APT44 has utilized a script named WAVESIGN, and the Android malware Infamous Chisel, attributed to APT44, to search for Signal's local database files. Turla, tracked by Microsoft as [Secret Blizzard](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/01d15f655c45c517f52235d63932fb377c319176239426681412afb01bf39dcc), and UNC1151, which overlaps with activity Microsoft tracks as [Storm-0257](https://sip.security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/36d4af836d2bd214b2f2a23da56c86bb6f4ab65663ee71869ac6356068f3c090), have used PowerShell scripts and Robocopy, respectively, to steal Signal messages. 

The targeting of Signal is likely driven by wartime demands to access sensitive government and military communications amid Russia's re-invasion of Ukraine. However, GTIG assesses that the tactics and methods used to target Signal will become more widespread in the near term, extending to additional threat actors and regions beyond the Ukrainian conflict zone.

## Microsoft Analysis and Additional OSINT Context
Recent reporting highlights a broader trend of cyber threat actors increasingly using Signal as part of malware campaigns—both as a social engineering tool and a direct target for compromise. For example, in February, [Volexity identified](https://sip.security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/7380b2ad) multiple Russian threat actors—including CozyLarch (tracked by Microsoft as Midnight Blizzard), UTA0304, and UTA0307—leveraging Device Code Authentication phishing to compromise Microsoft 365 accounts. These social engineering and spear-phishing campaigns, active since mid-January 2025, further underscore the growing focus on exploiting secure messaging platforms and identity management systems. Additionally in November, [BlackBerry detailed](https://sip.security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/a1778f1d) significant updates to the LightSpy malware campaign, which now includes advanced data-stealing capabilities affecting widely used communication apps. BlackBerry assesses with high confidence that LightSpy’s developers are linked to APT41 (tracked by Microsoft as Brass Typhoon), a Chinese cyber espionage group. The campaign introduced a Windows-based surveillance framework called DeepData, which features twelve modular plugins designed for extensive data theft from platforms such as WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal, and Outlook.

## Recommendations
Microsoft recommends the following to protect mobile devices:

- Implement [Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) on Android and iOS, which includes anti-phishing capabilities that also apply to QR code phishing attacks, blocking phishing sites from being accessed.
- Never click on unknown links received through ads, SMS messages, emails, or similar untrusted sources.
- Only install applications from trusted sources and official stores.
- If a device is no longer receiving updates, strongly consider replacing it with a new device.
- Always keep Install unknown apps disabled on the Android device to prevent apps from being installed from unknown sources.
- Avoid granting SMS permissions, notification listener access, or accessibility access to any applications without a strong understanding of why the application needs it. These are powerful permissions that are not commonly needed.
- Use the [Attack Simulator](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/attack-simulation-training-get-started?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in Microsoft Defender for Office 365 to run realistic, yet safe, simulated phishing and password attack campaigns. Utilize the [QR code payload](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/attack-simulation-training-payloads#qr-code-payloads?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in attack simulation training scenarios to mirror threat actor’s QR code spear-phishing techniques.

## References
[Signals of Trouble: Multiple Russia-Aligned Threat Actors Actively Targeting Signal Messenger](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/russia-targeting-signal-messenger/) Google Threat Intelligence Group (accessed 2025-02-19)

title: #StopRansomware: Ghost (Cring) Ransomware
content:
## Snapshot
Ghost ransomware actors, believed to be originating from China, have been actively exploiting vulnerabilities in internet-facing services running outdated software and firmware since early 2021, affecting organizations across over 70 countries in sectors such as critical infrastructure, healthcare, government, and various businesses.

## Description
They have targeted a wide range of entities, including religious institutions, technology and manufacturing companies, and small- and medium-sized businesses. The threat actors gain initial access through known vulnerabilities such as CVE-2018-13379, CVE-2010-2861, CVE-2009-3960, CVE-2021-34473, CVE-2021-34523, and CVE-2021-31207, often associated with the ProxyShell attack chain in Fortinet FortiOS, Adobe ColdFusion, Microsoft SharePoint, and Microsoft Exchange.

Once inside a network, Ghost actors upload web shells to compromised servers and use Windows Command Prompt or PowerShell to download and execute Cobalt Strike Beacon malware. They have been observed creating new accounts, changing passwords, and deploying web shells for persistence. They escalate privileges using tools like SharpZeroLogon and Mimikatz, and evade defenses by disabling antivirus software. For lateral movement and discovery, they use Cobalt Strike commands, WMIC, and PowerShell. They claim to exfiltrate data in ransom notes, but actual exfiltration is typically limited, often using Cobalt Strike Team Servers or web shells for exfiltration.

Command and control activities are conducted using direct IP addresses, web protocols, and encrypted email services for communication with victims. The ransomware executables used by Ghost actors include Cring.exe, Ghost.exe, ElysiumO.exe, and Locker.exe, which encrypt entire systems or specific directories, clear Windows Event Logs, and delete shadow copies to prevent recovery. The impact of their ransomware varies, with hardened systems often leading them to seek other targets. They have also been known to use TOX IDs in ransom notes as an alternative communication method with victims since August 2024. The ransom demanded can range from tens to hundreds of thousands of dollars, and the ransomware avoids encrypting files that could render devices inoperable. Ghost actors employ a suite of tools for their operations, including IOX, SharpShares.exe, SharpGPPPass.exe, SpnDump.exe, NBT.exe, BadPotato.exe, God.exe, HFS, and Ladon 911, for host discovery, exploiting vulnerabilities, privilege escalation, maintaining persistence.

## Microsoft Analysis and Additional OSINT Context
Following the recent joint advisory AA25-050A by the FBI, CISA, and MS-ISAC on Ghost (Cring) ransomware, cybersecurity firms have provided additional insights.[AttackIQ released](https://www.attackiq.com/2025/02/20/cisa-aa25-050a-ghost-cring-ransomware/) an attack graph emulating the ransomware's tactics, techniques, and procedures to help organizations assess their defenses.   
Similarly, [Picus Security highlighted](https://www.picussecurity.com/resource/blog/ghost-ransomware-analysis-cisa-alert-aa25-050a) Ghost's emergence in early 2021, noting its exploitation of known vulnerabilities in internet-facing services and its impact on organizations across over 70 countries.  These analyses underscore the importance of applying timely security updates and maintaining regular system backups to mitigate such threats.

## Recommendations
Apply these mitigations to reduce the impact of this threat. Check the recommendations card for the deployment status of monitored mitigations.

- Educate users about [preventing malware infections](https://www.microsoft.com/security/business/security-101/what-is-malware?ocid=magicti_ta_abbreviatedmktgpage"%20\t%20"_blank), such as ignoring or deleting unsolicited and unexpected emails or attachments sent through instant messaging applications or social networks as well as suspicious phone calls.
- Invest in advanced anti-phishing solutions that monitor incoming emails and visited websites. [Microsoft Defender for Office 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender/microsoft-365-security-center-mdo?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) brings together incident and alert management across email, devices, and identities, centralizing investigations for email-based threats.
- Apply Microsoft’s [security best practices for Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/MicrosoftTeams/teams-security-best-practices-for-safer-messaging) to safeguard Teams users.
- Consider [blocking or uninstalling](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/client-management/client-tools/quick-assist#disable-quick-assist-within-your-organization) Quick Assist and other remote monitoring and management tools if these tools are not in use in your environment. Apply mitigations listed in [Microsoft’s technique profile on abuse of remote monitoring and management tools](https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/44b8f927-5ab5-46bb-bb79-7ca2d4e30156/overview).
- Turn on [cloud-delivered protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/configure-block-at-first-sight-microsoft-defender-antivirus?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in Microsoft Defender Antivirus or the equivalent for your antivirus product to cover rapidly evolving attacker tools and techniques. Cloud-based machine learning protections block a huge majority of new and unknown variants.
- Turn on [tamper protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/prevent-changes-to-security-settings-with-tamper-protection?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) features to prevent attackers from stopping security services.
- Run [EDR in block mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/edr-in-block-mode?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) so that Microsoft Defender for Endpoint can block malicious artifacts, even when your non-Microsoft antivirus doesn’t detect the threat or when Microsoft Defender Antivirus is running in passive mode. EDR in block mode works behind the scenes to remediate malicious artifacts that are detected post-breach.
- Enable [network protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/enable-network-protection?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to prevent applications or users from accessing malicious domains and other malicious content on the internet.
- Enable [investigation and remediation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/automated-investigations?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in full automated mode to allow Microsoft Defender for Endpoint to take immediate action on alerts to resolve breaches, significantly reducing alert volume.
- Use [device discovery](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/device-discovery?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to increase your visibility into your network by finding unmanaged devices on your network and onboarding them to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
- Refer to [Microsoft’s human-operated ransomware overview](https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/05658b6c-dc62-496d-ad3c-c6a795a33c27/analystreport) for general hardening recommendations against ransomware attacks.

Microsoft Defender XDR customers can turn on [attack surface reduction rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to prevent common attack techniques used in ransomware attacks. Attack surface reduction rules are sweeping settings that are effective at stopping entire classes of threats:

- Ransom and lateral movement stage:
    - [Block process creations originating from PsExec and WMI commands](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-process-creations-originating-from-psexec-and-wmi-commands)
    - [Block executable files from running unless they meet a prevalence, age, or trusted list criterion](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-executable-files-from-running-unless-they-meet-a-prevalence-age-or-trusted-list-criterion)
    - [Use advanced protection against ransomware](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#use-advanced-protection-against-ransomware)
    - [Block credential stealing from the Windows local security authority subsystem (lsass.exe)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-credential-stealing-from-the-windows-local-security-authority-subsystem)
- Common techniques:
    - [Block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-execution-of-potentially-obfuscated-scripts)
    - [Block JavaScript or VBScript from launching downloaded executable content](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-javascript-or-vbscript-from-launching-downloaded-executable-content)
- Common entry vectors:
    - [Block all Office applications from creating child processes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-all-office-applications-from-creating-child-processes)
    - [Block Office communication application from creating child processes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-office-communication-application-from-creating-child-processes)
    - [Block Office applications from creating executable content](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-office-applications-from-injecting-code-into-other-processes)
    - [Block Office applications from injecting code into other processes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-office-applications-from-injecting-code-into-other-processes)

**Assess rule impact before deployment**

You can assess how an attack surface reduction rule might impact your network by opening the [security recommendation](https://security.microsoft.com/security-recommendations?ocid=magicti_ta_tvmsecreco) for that rule in threat and vulnerability management. In the recommendation details pane, check the user impact to determine what percentage of your devices can accept a new policy enabling the rule in blocking mode without adverse impact to user productivity.

*Security recommendations in threat and vulnerability management*

title: Zhong Stealer Analysis: New Malware Targeting Fintech and Cryptocurrency

## Snapshot
In December 2024, researchers at Any.Run identified a phishing campaign targeting the cryptocurrency and fintech industries, distributing a new stealer malware dubbed Zhong Stealer. The final stage involves harvesting browser credentials—starting with Brave and Edge—and exfiltrating this data via port 1131 to its C2 server. title: Highly Obfuscated .NET sectopRAT Mimic as Chrome Extension
content:
## Snapshot
Researchers at GBHackers have reported on [SectopRAT](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/23c4c2dd67e084e3ee74068eed3cd1659ea7b2aacd21ccd13ea6bddddca9f787), also known as Arechclient2, a Remote Access Trojan (RAT) that has recently been found to disguise itself as a legitimate Google Chrome extension named "Google Docs." This malware, developed using the .NET framework, is particularly difficult to analyze and detect due to its advanced obfuscation techniques, including the use of the calli obfuscator.

## Description
Despite challenges in deobfuscation, researchers have identified that SectopRAT can steal browser data, profile victim systems, target specific applications, and scan for cryptocurrency wallets and FTP credentials. SectopRAT communicates with its Command and Control (C2) server using encrypted channels over ports 9000 and 15647. The fake Chrome extension downloads files from its C2 server, enabling it to inject malicious scripts into web pages, capture user inputs, and transmit stolen data back to the attackers. SectopRAT's capabilities as an infostealer and remote control tool, along with its anti-analysis features such as anti-virtual machine mechanisms and encrypted C2 communication, make it a significant threat. The malware's ability to mimic legitimate software while evading detection underscores the evolving tactics of cybercriminals in leveraging trusted platforms to deploy highly evasive malware.

## Recommendations
Microsoft recommends the following mitigations to reduce the impact of this threat. Check the recommendations card for the deployment status of monitored mitigations. 
 
- Run [endpoint detection and response (EDR) in block mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/edr-in-block-mode?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) so that Microsoft Defender for Endpoint can block malicious artifacts, even when your non-Microsoft antivirus does not detect the threat or when Microsoft Defender Antivirus is running in passive mode. EDR in block mode works behind the scenes to remediate malicious artifacts that are detected post-breach.
- Configure [investigation and remediation](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/automated-investigations?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in full automated mode to let Microsoft Defender for Endpoint take immediate action on alerts to resolve breaches, significantly reducing alert volume.
- Encourage users to use Microsoft Edge and other web browsers that support [SmartScreen](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/threat-protection/microsoft-defender-smartscreen/microsoft-defender-smartscreen-overview?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc), which identifies and blocks malicious websites, including phishing sites, scam sites, and sites that contain exploits and host malware.
- Turn on [cloud-delivered protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/configure-block-at-first-sight-microsoft-defender-antivirus) in Microsoft Defender Antivirus, or the equivalent for your antivirus product, to cover rapidly evolving attacker tools and techniques. Cloud-based machine learning protections block a majority of new and unknown variants.
- Enable [network protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/enable-network-protection?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc).

Microsoft Defender customers can turn on attack surface reduction rules to prevent common attack techniques:

title: An Update on Fake Updates: Two New Actors, and New Mac Malware
content:
## Snapshot
Proofpoint recently identified two new cybercriminal groups, TA2726 and TA2727, involved in web inject campaigns to distribute malware.

## Description
These campaigns typically use malicious JavaScript, traffic distribution services (TDS), and payload downloads to compromise devices. Historically, TA569 dominated this landscape with its SocGholish fake update lures, but since 2023, multiple copycat actors have emerged, complicating threat tracking. Proofpoint observed that TA2726 operates a TDS, redirecting traffic to TA569 in North America and to TA2727 elsewhere, distributing [Lumma Stealer](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/33933578825488511c30b0728dd3c4f8b5ca20e41c285a56f796eb39f57531ad), [DeerStealer](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/e7fcb5fc), Marcher, and a new MacOS malware called FrigidStealer.
 
TA2727, financially motivated, likely buys traffic from forums and was recently seen delivering fake update lures tailored by region and device type. In a January 2025 campaign, Windows users saw MSI files with DOILoader and [Lumma Stealer](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/33933578825488511c30b0728dd3c4f8b5ca20e41c285a56f796eb39f57531ad), while Android users received the Marcher banking trojan. MacOS users were redirected to a fake update page that delivered FrigidStealer, a Go-based information stealer that exfiltrates browser cookies, cryptocurrency wallets, and Apple Notes.
 
FrigidStealer uses social engineering techniques, including Gatekeeper bypasses and password prompts, to appear legitimate and steal sensitive data. Proofpoint researchers identified the infrastructure behind these campaigns, noting consistent patterns in domains, IP addresses, and traffic redirection techniques.
 
According to Proofpoint, the growing complexity of web inject campaigns is attributed to stronger defenses against email-based malware and network exploitation, forcing threat actors to shift tactics.

## Recommendations
Microsoft recommends the following mitigations to reduce the impact of this threat. Check the recommendations card for the deployment status of monitored mitigations.  

- Encourage users to use Microsoft Edge and other web browsers that support [SmartScreen](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/web-protection-overview?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc), which identifies and blocks malicious websites, including phishing sites, scam sites, and sites that contain exploits and host malware.
- Practice the principle of least privilege and maintain credential hygiene. Avoid the use of domain-wide, administrator-level service accounts. Restricting local administrative privileges can help limit installation of RATs and other unwanted applications.
- [Enable network protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/enable-network-protection) to prevent users from accessing dangerous domains through applications. Network protection will block all outbound HTTP(s) traffic that attempts to connect to low-reputation sources (based on the domain or hostname).
- Turn on [cloud-delivered protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/enable-cloud-protection-microsoft-defender-antivirus?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) and automatic sample submission on Microsoft Defender Antivirus. These capabilities use artificial intelligence and machine learning to quickly identify and stop new and unknown threats.
- Turn on [tamper protection features](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/prevent-changes-to-security-settings-with-tamper-protection?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to prevent attackers from stopping security services.
- For additional recommendations on hardening your organization against ransomware attacks, refer to our [threat overview on human-operated ransomware](https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/05658b6c-dc62-496d-ad3c-c6a795a33c27/analystreport?ocid=magicti_ta_ta2).   
  
Microsoft Defender customers can turn on [attack surface reduction rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to prevent common attack techniques:

- [Block executable files from running unless they meet a prevalence, age, or trusted list criterion](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-executable-files-from-running-unless-they-meet-a-prevalence-age-or-trusted-list-criterion)
- [Block JavaScript or VBScript from launching downloaded executable content](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-javascript-or-vbscript-from-launching-downloaded-executable-content)
- [Turn on PUA protection in block mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/detect-block-potentially-unwanted-apps-microsoft-defender-antivirus?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc)
- [Use advanced protection against ransomware](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#use-advanced-protection-against-ransomware)

## Detections/Hunting Queries

### Microsoft Defender Antivirus
Microsoft Defender Antivirus detects threat components as the following malware:
 
- [Trojan:MacOS/Multiverze](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=Trojan:MacOS/Multiverze)
- [Program:MacOS/Multiverze](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=Program:MacOS/Multiverze)
- [Trojan:Win32/Malgent!MSR](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=Trojan:Win32/Malgent!MSR)
- Trojan:AndroidOS/Multiverze

title: Rhadamanthys Infostealer Being Distributed Through MSC Extension
content:
## Snapshot
AhnLab Security Intelligence Center (ASEC) has confirmed the distribution of Rhadamanthys [Infostealer](https://sip.security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/2296d491ea381b532b24f2575f9418d4b6723c17b8a1f507d20c2140a75d16d6) malware, which is being spread through files with the MSC extension. These files are executed by the Microsoft Management Console (MMC) and can perform various tasks such as script code and command execution.

## Description
The MSC malware has been increasingly distributed since June 2024, according to AhnLab, and falls into two categories: one that exploits a vulnerability in apds.dll ([CVE-2024-43572](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/cves/CVE-2024-43572/)) and another that uses Console Taskpad to execute commands. Although [a patch was released](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2024-43572) in October, the apds.dll vulnerability exploit is the most common. The apds.dll exploit involves accessing a resource named "redirect.html" within the DLL and executing code directly within it, bypassing MMC. 

The Console Taskpad method, on the other hand, executes commands within MMC using features supported by MMC, which allows for the execution of simple commands and specific files. The malicious MSC file is disguised as an MS Word document and, upon clicking the "Open" button, downloads and executes a PowerShell script from an external source. This script contains the Rhadamanthys executable, which is then created and executed under the %LocalAppData% directory with the name "eRSg.mp3".

## Microsoft Analysis and Additional OSINT Context
Rhadamanthys continues to evolve, maintaining a steady presence in cybercriminal activity through new tactics and social engineering campaigns. In January, [Proofpoint researchers observed](https://sip.security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/e3cac3e6) tax-themed phishing attacks leveraging fake HMRC and Intuit messages to distribute Rhadamanthys alongside other malware like zgRAT. And in November 2024, [Check Point Research uncovered](https://sip.security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/d2caadf2) the "CopyRh(ight)adamantys" campaign, which used copyright infringement lures and AI-assisted localization to enhance phishing effectiveness. Meanwhile, [Recorded Future detailed](https://sip.security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/c9ea8588) the malware’s latest version, 0.7.0, which introduces AI-driven optical character recognition (OCR) to extract cryptocurrency seed phrases and new evasion tactics, such as MSI-based execution.

## Recommendations
Microsoft recommends the following mitigations to reduce the impact infostealer threats:
 
- Check your Office 365 email filtering settings to ensure you block spoofed emails, spam, and emails with malware. Use [Microsoft Defender for Office 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/defender-for-office-365?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) for enhanced phishing protection and coverage against new threats and polymorphic variants. Configure Microsoft Defender for Office 365 to [recheck links on click](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/safe-links-about?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) and [delete sent mail](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/zero-hour-auto-purge?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in response to newly acquired threat intelligence. Turn on [safe attachments policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/safe-attachments-policies-configure?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to check attachments to inbound email.
- Encourage users to use Microsoft Edge and other web browsers that support [SmartScreen](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/web-protection-overview?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc), which identifies and blocks malicious websites, including phishing sites, scam sites, and sites that host malware.
- Turn on [cloud-delivered protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/configure-block-at-first-sight-microsoft-defender-antivirus?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in Microsoft Defender Antivirus, or the equivalent for your antivirus product, to cover rapidly evolving attacker tools and techniques. Cloud-based machine learning protections block a majority of new and unknown variants.
- Enforce MFA on all accounts, remove users excluded from MFA, and strictly [require MFA](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/identity-protection/howto-identity-protection-configure-mfa-policy?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) from all devices, in all locations, at all times.
- Enable passwordless authentication methods (for example, Windows Hello, FIDO keys, or Microsoft Authenticator) for accounts that support passwordless. For accounts that still require passwords, use authenticator apps like Microsoft Authenticator for MFA. [Refer to this article](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/authentication/concept-authentication-methods?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) for the different authentication methods and features.
- For MFA that uses authenticator apps, ensure that the app requires a code to be typed in where possible, as many intrusions where MFA was enabled still succeeded due to users clicking “Yes” on the prompt on their phones even when they were not at their [devices](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/authentication/how-to-mfa-number-match?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc). Refer to [this article](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/authentication/concept-authentication-methods?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) for an example.
- Remind employees that enterprise or workplace credentials should not be stored in browsers or password vaults secured with personal credentials. Organizations can turn off password syncing in browser on managed devices using [Group Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/microsoft-edge-enterprise-sync#sync-group-policies?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc).

Microsoft Defender customers can [turn on attack surface reduction rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to prevent common attack techniques used in infostealer infections. Attack surface reduction rules are sweeping settings that stop entire classes of threats including, infostealers, credential theft, and ransomware. The following bullet points offer more guidance on specific mitigation advice:

- [Turn on PUA protection in block mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/detect-block-potentially-unwanted-apps-microsoft-defender-antivirus?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc)
- [Block executable files from running unless they meet a prevalence, age, or trusted list criterion](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-executable-files-from-running-unless-they-meet-a-prevalence-age-or-trusted-list-criterion)
- [Block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-execution-of-potentially-obfuscated-scripts)

## Detections/Hunting Queries

### Microsoft Defender Antivirus
Microsoft Defender Antivirus detects threat components as the following malware:

- [Trojan:Win32/Rhadamanthys](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=Trojan:Win32/Rhadamanthys!MTB&threatId=-2147127827&ocid=magicti_ta_ency)
- Trojan:Win32/Alevaul

### Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
Alerts with the following titles in the security center can indicate threat activity on your network:
 
- Information stealing malware activity

title: Open Spoofing
content:
## Snapshot
Mimecast researchers identified recent phishing campaigns exploiting ISP email infrastructure. By leveraging compromised consumer routers, the threat actor bypasses authentication controls, enabling high-volume spoofing of trusted brands to harvest credentials.

## Description
Mimecast researchers attribute the campaign to threat group TO3028, whom they identify as a sophisticated threat actor specializing in email security exploitation and credential harvesting. The group leverages advanced delivery techniques, systematic testing, and high-volume phishing campaigns to bypass defenses and maintain persistent access to compromised systems.
 
TO3028 exploits ISP email services using compromised consumer routers as proxy servers. This technique allows attackers to send phishing emails at scale without requiring authentication, bypassing traditional security measures. The campaign primarily targets user credentials by spoofing well-known brands such as BBC, CNN, and DocuSign. Attackers employ obfuscated redirection chains involving legitimate domains to evade detection, ultimately directing victims to credential-harvesting pages hosted on Microsoft’s Azure infrastructure. Mimicast reports that this activity, which escalated significantly in late 2024, highlights systemic weaknesses in ISP-managed email systems, particularly around weak authentication and insufficient monitoring.

## Recommendations
Microsoft recommends the following mitigations to reduce the impact of this threat. 

- Check your Office 365 email filtering settings to ensure you block spoofed emails, spam, and emails with malware. Use [Microsoft Defender for Office 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/defender-for-office-365?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) for enhanced phishing protection and coverage against new threats and polymorphic variants. - [Most domains sending mail](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/microsoftdefenderforoffice365blog/business-email-uncompromised---part-three/2247693) to Office 365 lack valid DMARC enforcement, making them susceptible to spoofing. Microsoft 365 and Exchange Online Protection (EOP) mitigate this risk by detecting forged "From" headers to block spoofed emails and prevent credential theft. [Spoof Intelligence](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/anti-spoofing-spoof-intelligence), enabled by default, adds an extra layer of security by identifying spoofed senders
- [User Impersonation Protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/anti-phishing-policies-about?view=o365-worldwide#user-impersonation-protection) prevents attackers from spoofing specific internal or external email addresses by verifying messages against a protected sender list. Cloud-based machine learning protections block a majority of new and unknown variants.

Microsoft Defender customers can [turn on attack surface reduction rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to prevent common attack techniques used in infostealer infections. title: JavaScript to Command-and-Control (C2) Server Malware
content:
## Snapshot
Researchers at CYFIRMA identified a malware campaign leveraging sophisticated obfuscation and multi-stage execution to evade detection.

## Description
It starts with an obfuscated JavaScript file that retrieves encoded commands from an open-source service, which then triggers a PowerShell script. This script downloads an image and a text file, both of which contain hidden malicious executables using advanced steganographic techniques.
 
Once executed, the malware deploys an information stealer that extracts sensitive system credentials and transmits them to an attacker-controlled Telegram bot, bypassing traditional security measures. The attack chain is highly evasive, using techniques such as reflective loading, obfuscation, and abuse of legitimate cloud services to blend into normal network traffic.
 
The campaign exploits legacy technologies like ActiveX and Windows Script Host (WSH) to execute commands, while PowerShell enables dynamic payload execution and network communication. Attackers further use Base64 encoding and custom decoding functions to conceal malicious code. The malware is designed to steal credentials from browsers, communication platforms, and cryptocurrency wallets, exfiltrating data through encrypted Telegram communications.
 
The attack infrastructure, including jilas.net as a payload host, suggests a compromised or attacker-controlled domain. This highlights the importance of proactive threat intelligence, network monitoring, and endpoint detection strategies to combat evolving threats. CYFIRMA recommends that organizations focus on restricting execution of unauthorized scripts, monitoring outbound network traffic, and implementing behavioral-based detection mechanisms to prevent such attacks.

## Recommendations
Microsoft recommends the following mitigations to reduce the impact of this threat.
 
- Turn on [cloud-delivered protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/linux-preferences) in Microsoft Defender Antivirus or the equivalent for your antivirus product to cover rapidly evolving attacker tools and techniques. Cloud-based machine learning protections block a majority of new and unknown threats.
- Run [EDR in block mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/edr-in-block-mode?view=o365-worldwide?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) so that Microsoft Defender for Endpoint can block malicious artifacts, even when your non-Microsoft antivirus does not detect the threat or when Microsoft Defender Antivirus is running in passive mode. EDR in block mode works behind the scenes to remediate malicious artifacts that are detected post-breach.
- Allow [investigation and remediation](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/automated-investigations?view=o365-worldwide?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in full automated mode to allow Microsoft Defender for Endpoint to take immediate action on alerts to resolve breaches, significantly reducing alert volume.
- [Enable](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/enable-controlled-folders) controlled folder access.
- Ensure that [tamper protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/prevent-changes-to-security-settings-with-tamper-protection#how-do-i-configure-or-manage-tamper-protection) is enabled in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
- Enable [network protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/enable-network-protection) in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
- Follow the credential hardening recommendations in the [on-premises credential theft overview](https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/9382203e-5155-4b5e-af74-21562b1004d5/analystreport) to defend against common credential theft techniques like LSASS access.
- [Enable](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference#block-credential-stealing-from-the-windows-local-security-authority-subsystem) LSA protection.

## Detections/Hunting Queries

### Microsoft Defender Antivirus
Microsoft Defender Antivirus detects threat components as the following malware:
 
- [Trojan:Win32/Leonem](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=Trojan:Win32/Leonem)

title: Malicious PirateFi game infects Steam users with Vidar malware
content:
## Snapshot
The free-to-play game PirateFi, available on the Steam store, was found to be distributing the Vidar infostealing malware.

## Description
The game, developed by Seaworth Interactive, was downloaded by up to 1,500 users between February 6th and February 12th before Steam discovered the malware and removed the game. Steam has since been [alerting](https://x.com/SteamDB/status/1889610974484705314) users who downloaded the game, suggesting they run a full system scan and consider reinstalling their operating system. Marius Genheimer from SECUINFRA Falcon Team analyzed a sample of the malware and confirmed it as a version of Vidar. The malware was concealed within a file named Pirate.exe, which contained a payload called Howard.exe, packed with the InnoSetup installer. The threat actor behind this had altered the game files multiple times, employing various obfuscation techniques and modifying the command-and-control servers used for stealing credentials. The Vidar [infostealer](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/2296d491ea381b532b24f2575f9418d4b6723c17b8a1f507d20c2140a75d16d6) is known to compromise sensitive information such as credentials, session cookies, and secrets stored in browsers, email clients, and cryptocurrency wallets. The name PirateFi, with references to web3, blockchain, and cryptocurrency, appears to have been chosen to attract a specific demographic of players.

This incident is not the first time malware has infiltrated the Steam store. This incident follows previous instances where Steam users were targeted by malware, such as malicious [Dota 2 game modes in February 2023](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/malicious-dota-2-game-modes-infected-players-with-malware/) and a compromised mod for [Slay the Spire in December 2023](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/steam-game-mod-breached-to-push-password-stealing-malware/). Despite Steam's efforts to introduce additional security measures, the PirateFi case demonstrates that these are not always effective in preventing malware distribution.

## Microsoft Analysis and Additional OSINT Context
[Active since at least 2018](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/9d955e01), Vidar is an infostealer reportedly operating as a Malware-as-a-Service (MaaS) model, written in C++, and frequently updated. [Cyfrima reports](https://www.cyfirma.com/research/vidar-stealer-an-in-depth-analysis-of-an-information-stealing-malware/) that its MaaS operations use Russian, and[ANY.RUN notes](https://any.run/malware-trends/vidar) that Vidar halts execution if the targeted device is in the ex-USSR or has a Russian keyboard.
 
Potentially a copycat or fork of the Arkei malware, Vidar is designed to steal a wide range of sensitive information — from text files and credentials stored in browsers to banking details, credit card information, and cryptocurrency wallets. It can take screenshots, record private messages, and, according to ANY.RUN, steal data from Tor. [Check Point researchers highlight](https://www.checkpoint.com/cyber-hub/threat-prevention/what-is-malware/what-is-vidar-malware/) it can also act as a downloader for other malware.

Vidar leverages social media platforms like Telegram and Steam for command-and-control (C2) communication. Initially executed via a malicious download, it spawns a child process to collect device data and can potentially delete itself post-attack. Additionally, attackers can update C2 IPs/URLs embedded in social media profiles to evade detection.

Vidar often operates with other malware strains. Recent reports include:
 
- [April 2024](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/9b8597c1): Proofpoint found Vidar, StealC, and Lumma Stealer distributed via YouTube, disguised as pirated software and video game cracks.
- [September 2024](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/e0fff69a): Secureworks CTU reported fake "Verify You Are Human" prompts after searching Google for video streaming services, Vidar and StealC to steal online services and corporate network credentials, later sold on Russian markets.
- [October 2024](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/7468eeaa): Elastic Security Labs identified Vidar and StealC bypassing Chrome's Application-Bound Encryption to extract unencrypted cookies.
- [January 2025](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/7644c05b): Trend Micro's Managed XDR identified a cyberattack campaign leveraging GitHub’s release infrastructure to distribute Vidar, SectopRAT, and Lumma Stealer. Vidar stole data from various browsers and cloud storage services.

[In June 2024](https://www.cyfirma.com/research/vidar-stealer-an-in-depth-analysis-of-an-information-stealing-malware/), Cyfirma reported Vidar’s is supported by a dedicated team that provides weekly functionality updates on a dark web portal.

## Recommendations
Microsoft recommends the following mitigations to reduce the impact of [Information Stealer](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/2296d491ea381b532b24f2575f9418d4b6723c17b8a1f507d20c2140a75d16d6) threats. 

- Check your Office 365 email filtering settings to ensure you block spoofed emails, spam, and emails with malware. Use [Microsoft Defender for Office 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/defender-for-office-365?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) for enhanced phishing protection and coverage against new threats and polymorphic variants. Configure Microsoft Defender for Office 365 to [recheck links on click](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/safe-links-about?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) and [delete sent mail](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/zero-hour-auto-purge?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in response to newly acquired threat intelligence. Turn on [safe attachments policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/safe-attachments-policies-configure?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to check attachments to inbound email.
- Encourage users to use Microsoft Edge and other web browsers that support [SmartScreen](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/web-protection-overview?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc), which identifies and blocks malicious websites, including phishing sites, scam sites, and sites that host malware.
- Turn on [cloud-delivered protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/configure-block-at-first-sight-microsoft-defender-antivirus?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in Microsoft Defender Antivirus, or the equivalent for your antivirus product, to cover rapidly evolving attacker tools and techniques. Cloud-based machine learning protections block a majority of new and unknown variants.
- Enforce MFA on all accounts, remove users excluded from MFA, and strictly [require MFA](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/identity-protection/howto-identity-protection-configure-mfa-policy?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) from all devices, in all locations, at all times.
- Enable passwordless authentication methods (for example, Windows Hello, FIDO keys, or Microsoft Authenticator) for accounts that support passwordless. For accounts that still require passwords, use authenticator apps like Microsoft Authenticator for MFA. Learn [what authentication and verification methods are available in Microsoft Entra ID.](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-authentication-methods)
- For MFA that uses authenticator apps, ensure that the app requires a code to be typed in where possible, as many intrusions where MFA was enabled still succeeded due to users clicking “Yes” on the prompt on their phones even when they were not at their [devices](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/authentication/how-to-mfa-number-match?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc).
- For information on password management for Microsoft Edge read ["Microsoft Edge password manager security."](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/deployedge/microsoft-edge-security-password-manager-security)

Microsoft Defender customers can [turn on attack surface reduction rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to prevent common attack techniques used in infostealer infections. Attack surface reduction rules are sweeping settings that stop entire classes of threats including, infostealers, credential theft, and ransomware. The following bullet points offer more guidance on specific mitigation advice: 

- [Turn on PUA protection in block mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/detect-block-potentially-unwanted-apps-microsoft-defender-antivirus?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc)
- [Block executable files from running unless they meet a prevalence, age, or trusted list criterion](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-executable-files-from-running-unless-they-meet-a-prevalence-age-or-trusted-list-criterion)
- [Block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-execution-of-potentially-obfuscated-scripts)

## Detections/Hunting Queries

### Microsoft Defender Antivirus
- [Trojan:Win32/Vidar](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=Trojan:Win32/Vidar.PAZ!MTB)
- [PWS:Win32/Vidar](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=PWS:Win32/Vidar.YB!MTB)
- [Trojan:MSIL/Vidar](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=Trojan:MSIL/Vidar.PTAX!MTB)

[Arkei Variants: From Vidar to Mars Stealer](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/9d955e01). Microsoft (accessed 2025-02-20)

title: XELERA Ransomware Campaign: Fake Food Corporation of India Job Offers Targeting Tech Aspirants
content:
#### Targeted Geolocations
- India



## Snapshot
Researchers at Seqrite Labs have uncovered a number of campaigns leveraging fake job descriptions that lead to the deployment of Xelera ransomware.

## Description
These attacks specifically target job seekers applying for technical positions at the Food Corporation of India (FCI). The malware is delivered via a malicious Word document, FCEI-job-notification.doc, which contains embedded code that executes a PyInstaller-based executable, jobnotification2025.exe, upon opening. This executable launches Python scripts designed to exfiltrate data, disrupt system operations, and deploy ransomware.
 
Once executed, the malware establishes control via a Discord bot, enabling the attacker to steal browser credentials, exfiltrate files, and execute remote commands. The bot also facilitates privilege escalation, allowing the malware to run with administrative rights, lock or shut down the system, and perform other malicious activities. Additionally, the malware includes disruptive visual and sensory effects, such as screen distortions, blurring, and forced audio playback.
 
The final stage of the attack deploys the Xelera ransomware, which, rather than encrypting files, focuses on system corruption. It modifies the Master Boot Record (MBR) to render the system unbootable, terminates critical processes, and repeatedly displays ransom messages. The attacker demands payment in Litecoin, as evidenced by multiple transactions linked to the provided cryptocurrency wallet.
 
Seqrite Labs warns that Xelera is a new and evolving threat, combining data theft, system sabotage, and extortion. As it actively spreads, security professionals must remain vigilant against spear-phishing campaigns distributing fake job listings.

## Recommendations
Apply these mitigations to reduce the impact of this threat. Check the recommendations card for the deployment status of monitored mitigations.

- Educate users about [preventing malware infections](https://www.microsoft.com/security/business/security-101/what-is-malware?ocid=magicti_ta_abbreviatedmktgpage"%20\t%20"_blank), such as ignoring or deleting unsolicited and unexpected emails or attachments sent through instant messaging applications or social networks as well as suspicious phone calls.
- Invest in advanced anti-phishing solutions that monitor incoming emails and visited websites. [Microsoft Defender for Office 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender/microsoft-365-security-center-mdo?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) brings together incident and alert management across email, devices, and identities, centralizing investigations for email-based threats.
- Apply Microsoft’s [security best practices for Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/MicrosoftTeams/teams-security-best-practices-for-safer-messaging) to safeguard Teams users.
- Consider [blocking or uninstalling](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/client-management/client-tools/quick-assist#disable-quick-assist-within-your-organization) Quick Assist and other remote monitoring and management tools if these tools are not in use in your environment. Apply mitigations listed in [Microsoft’s technique profile on abuse of remote monitoring and management tools](https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/44b8f927-5ab5-46bb-bb79-7ca2d4e30156/overview).
- Turn on [cloud-delivered protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/configure-block-at-first-sight-microsoft-defender-antivirus?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in Microsoft Defender Antivirus or the equivalent for your antivirus product to cover rapidly evolving attacker tools and techniques. Cloud-based machine learning protections block a huge majority of new and unknown variants.
- Turn on [tamper protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/prevent-changes-to-security-settings-with-tamper-protection?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) features to prevent attackers from stopping security services.
- Run [EDR in block mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/edr-in-block-mode?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) so that Microsoft Defender for Endpoint can block malicious artifacts, even when your non-Microsoft antivirus doesn’t detect the threat or when Microsoft Defender Antivirus is running in passive mode. EDR in block mode works behind the scenes to remediate malicious artifacts that are detected post-breach.
- Enable [network protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/enable-network-protection?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to prevent applications or users from accessing malicious domains and other malicious content on the internet.
- Enable [investigation and remediation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/automated-investigations?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in full automated mode to allow Microsoft Defender for Endpoint to take immediate action on alerts to resolve breaches, significantly reducing alert volume.
- Use [device discovery](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/device-discovery?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to increase your visibility into your network by finding unmanaged devices on your network and onboarding them to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
- Refer to [Microsoft’s human-operated ransomware overview](https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/05658b6c-dc62-496d-ad3c-c6a795a33c27/analystreport) for general hardening recommendations against ransomware attacks.

Microsoft Defender XDR customers can turn on [attack surface reduction rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to prevent common attack techniques used in ransomware attacks. Attack surface reduction rules are sweeping settings that are effective at stopping entire classes of threats:

- Ransom and lateral movement stage:
    - [Block process creations originating from PsExec and WMI commands](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-process-creations-originating-from-psexec-and-wmi-commands)
    - [Block executable files from running unless they meet a prevalence, age, or trusted list criterion](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-executable-files-from-running-unless-they-meet-a-prevalence-age-or-trusted-list-criterion)
    - [Use advanced protection against ransomware](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#use-advanced-protection-against-ransomware)
    - [Block credential stealing from the Windows local security authority subsystem (lsass.exe)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-credential-stealing-from-the-windows-local-security-authority-subsystem)
- Common techniques:
    - [Block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-execution-of-potentially-obfuscated-scripts)
    - [Block JavaScript or VBScript from launching downloaded executable content](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-javascript-or-vbscript-from-launching-downloaded-executable-content)
- Common entry vectors:
    - [Block all Office applications from creating child processes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-all-office-applications-from-creating-child-processes)
    - [Block Office communication application from creating child processes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-office-communication-application-from-creating-child-processes)
    - [Block Office applications from creating executable content](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-office-applications-from-injecting-code-into-other-processes)
    - [Block Office applications from injecting code into other processes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-office-applications-from-injecting-code-into-other-processes)

## Detections/Hunting Queries

### Microsoft Defender Antivirus
Microsoft Defender Antivirus detects threat components as the following malware:
 
- [Trojan:Win32/Wacatac](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=Trojan:Win32/Wacatac.B!ml)
