title: New Supply Chain Attack Targeting Chrome Extensions to Inject Malicious Code
content:
## Snapshot
Skekoia reports sophisticated supply chain attack targeting Chrome browser extensions was discovered, affecting potentially hundreds of thousands of users.

## Description
The attack, which took place in December 2024, involved phishing campaigns against extension developers and the subsequent injection of malicious code into legitimate Chrome extensions. Sensitive user data, such as API keys, session cookies, and authentication tokens from services like ChatGPT and Facebook for Business, was exfiltrated.

The threat actor, active since at least 2023, shifted tactics in late 2024 from distributing fake extensions to compromising legitimate ones through phishing and malicious OAuth applications. The attackers used spear-phishing emails disguised as official notifications from the Chrome Web Store to trick developers into authorizing a malicious OAuth application named "Privacy Policy Extensions." These emails originated from domains mimicking legitimate Google services. Once developers granted permissions, the attackers could upload compromised versions of the extensions to the Chrome Web Store.

The malicious code included scripts like background.js, which exfiltrated sensitive data, and context\_responder.js, which harvested credentials from web pages visited by users. The attackers' infrastructure involved multiple domains registered via Namecheap and hosted on AS20473 (VULTR), with command-and-control servers hosting configuration files for the malicious scripts and subdomains likely storing the harvested data. Approximately 15 Chrome extensions were compromised, including Proxy SwitchyOmega, GraphQL Network Inspector, and VidHelper Video Download Helper. This incident highlights the evolving tactics of cybercriminals and the risks posed by compromised browser extensions.

## Microsoft Analysis and Additional OSINT Context
SEKOIA’s detailed analysis builds on Cyberhaven’s preliminary report, [which you can read here](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/8d2371e6), providing deeper insights into the methods used and the implications for cybersecurity. The two articles highlight critical cybersecurity risks associated with Chrome browser extensions. Customers should recognize the importance of scrutinizing browser extensions, ensuring strict security controls, and staying informed about emerging threats in this area to safeguard their systems and data.

## Recommendations
Microsoft recommends the following mitigations for related threats.

- Establish [best practices to secure software supply chain](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/concepts/security-best-practices).
- Conduct an [audit for packages and dependencies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/concepts/auditing-packages), analyzing the security of packages included in software projects.
- Configure [continuous access evaluation](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/conditional-access/concept-continuous-access-evaluation?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in your tenant.
- Invest in advanced anti-phishing solutions that monitor incoming emails and visited websites. [Microsoft Defender for Office](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender/microsoft-365-security-center-mdo?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) 365 brings together incident and alert management across email, devices, and identities, centralizing investigations for threats in email. To build resilience against phishing attacks in general, organizations can use [anti-phishing policies](https://docs.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/set-up-anti-phishing-policies?view=o365-worldwide) to enable mailbox intelligence settings, as well as configure impersonation protection settings for specific messages and sender domains. Enabling [SafeLinks](https://docs.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/safe-links?view=o365-worldwide) ensures real-time protection by scanning at time of delivery and at time of click.
- Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management Admins can conduct their own [Browser extensions assessment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-vulnerability-management/tvm-browser-extensions).

Defenders can also complement MFA with the following solutions and best practices to further protect their organizations from such attacks. 

- Use [security defaults](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/fundamentals/concept-fundamentals-security-defaults?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) as a baseline set of policies to improve identity security posture. For more granular control, enable conditional access policies. [Conditional access](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/conditional-access/overview?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) policies evaluate sign-in requests using additional identity-driven signals like user or group membership, IP location information, and device status, among others, and are enforced for suspicious sign-ins. Organizations can protect themselves from attacks that leverage stolen credentials by enabling policies such as compliant devices or trusted IP address requirements.
- Invest in advanced anti-phishing solutions that monitor and scan incoming emails and visited websites. For example, organizations can leverage web browsers that automatically [identify and block malicious websites](https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/microsoft-edge-security-smartscreen?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc), including those used in this phishing campaign, and solutions that [detect and block malicious emails, links, and files](https://www.microsoft.com/security/business/siem-and-xdr/microsoft-defender-office-365?ocid=magicti_ta_abbreviatedmktgpage). Additionally, block phishing websites and other malicious URLs and domains in the browser through [Microsoft Defender SmartScreen](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/virus-and-threat-protection/microsoft-defender-smartscreen/), as well as the detection of suspicious and malicious behavior on endpoints.

Microsoft Defender customers can [turn on attack surface reduction rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc). 

    - [Turn on PUA protection in block mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/detect-block-potentially-unwanted-apps-microsoft-defender-antivirus?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc)
    - [Block executable files from running unless they meet a prevalence, age, or trusted list criterion](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-executable-files-from-running-unless-they-meet-a-prevalence-age-or-trusted-list-criterion)
    - [Block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-execution-of-potentially-obfuscated-scripts)

title: Telegram captcha tricks you into running malicious PowerShell scripts
content:
## Snapshot
[Vx-underground](https://x.com/vxunderground/status/1881946956806926351) has identified a new cyberattack exploiting the news of Ross Ulbricht's pardon to lure individuals to a malicious Telegram channel.

## Description
Threat actors create fake but verified Ross Ulbricht accounts on the X platform to lure victims to malicious Telegram channels. Once on Telegram, users are subjected to a fake identity verification process called "Safeguard," which deceives them into copying and executing a PowerShell command. This command downloads a ZIP file containing multiple files. According to BleepingComputer, a comment on VirusTotal suggests that one of the files may function as a [Cobalt Strike](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/fd8511c1d61e93d39411acf36a31130a6795efe186497098fe0c6f2ccfb920fc) loader—a tool commonly employed by threat actors to establish remote access to devices, often paving the way for ransomware attacks and data theft.

This campaign is a variant of the ["ClickFix"](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/67d03ba9) tactic, where threat actors distribute malware by deceiving users into running code to fix common errors. This tactic has been increasingly used to distribute malware. In this case, the code is disguised as a captcha or verification process that users must complete to join the channel. Telegram has responded by stating that they proactively monitor and remove harmful content from their platform.

## Microsoft Analysis and Additional OSINT Context
In 2024, ClickFix was repeatedly reported as a tactic enabling attackers to bypass browser security and infiltrate systems undetected. [Researchers highlighted](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/67d03ba9) its global use and effectiveness in utilizing social engineering. The integration of Telegram verification further underscores ClickFix's ongoing appeal to threat actors.

## Recommendations
Microsoft recommends the following mitigations to reduce the impact of this threat.

- Turn on [cloud-delivered protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/linux-preferences) in Microsoft Defender Antivirus or the equivalent for your antivirus product to cover rapidly evolving attacker tools and techniques. Cloud-based machine learning protections block a majority of new and unknown threats.
- Run [EDR in block mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/edr-in-block-mode?view=o365-worldwide?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) so that Microsoft Defender for Endpoint can block malicious artifacts, even when your non-Microsoft antivirus does not detect the threat or when Microsoft Defender Antivirus is running in passive mode. EDR in block mode works behind the scenes to remediate malicious artifacts that are detected post-breach.
- Allow [investigation and remediation](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/automated-investigations?view=o365-worldwide?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in full automated mode to allow Microsoft Defender for Endpoint to take immediate action on alerts to resolve breaches, significantly reducing alert volume.
- [Enable](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/enable-controlled-folders) controlled folder access.
- Ensure that [tamper protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/prevent-changes-to-security-settings-with-tamper-protection#how-do-i-configure-or-manage-tamper-protection) is enabled in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
- Enable [network protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/enable-network-protection) in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
- Follow the credential hardening recommendations in the [on-premises credential theft overview](https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/9382203e-5155-4b5e-af74-21562b1004d5/analystreport) to defend against common credential theft techniques like LSASS access.

Microsoft Defender XDR customers can turn on the following [attack surface reduction rule](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction) to prevent common attack techniques used for ransomware.

- [Block](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference#block-executable-content-from-email-client-and-webmail) executable content from email client and webmail
- [Block](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference#block-executable-files-from-running-unless-they-meet-a-prevalence-age-or-trusted-list-criterion) executable files from running unless they meet a prevalence, age, or trusted list criterion

Additional guidance for CobaltStrike 

Guidance for end users 

- For more tips on how to keep your device safe, go to the [Microsoft security help & learning portal](https://support.microsoft.com/security).
- To learn more about preventing trojans or other malware from affecting individual devices, [read about preventing malware infection](https://www.microsoft.com/security/business/security-101/what-is-malware).

Guidance for enterprise administrators and Microsoft 365 Defender customers 

Apply these mitigations to reduce the impact of this threat. Check the recommendations card for the deployment status of monitored mitigations. 

- Enable [investigation and remediation](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/automated-investigations) in full automated mode to allow Microsoft Defender for Endpoint to take immediate action on alerts to resolve breaches, significantly reducing alert volume.
- Use [device discovery](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/device-discovery) to increase your visibility into your network by finding unmanaged devices on your network and onboarding them to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
- [Enable](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference#block-credential-stealing-from-the-windows-local-security-authority-subsystem) LSA protection.

title: Threat Actors Chained Vulnerabilities in Ivanti Cloud Service Applications
content:
## Snapshot
The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) and Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) released a joint Cybersecurity Advisory in response to the exploitation in September 2024 of vulnerabilities in Ivanti Cloud Service Appliances (CSA): CVE-2024-8190, CVE-2024-8963, CVE-2024-9379, and CVE-2024-9380.

## Description
Threat actors exploited these zero-day vulnerabilities in two distinct chains to gain initial access, execute remote code, obtain credentials, and implant webshells. The first chain combined [CVE-2024-8963](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/cves/CVE-2024-8963/) with [CVE-2024-8190](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/cves/CVE-2024-8190/) and [CVE-2024-9380](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/cves/CVE-2024-9380/), while the second used [CVE-2024-8963](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/cves/CVE-2024-8963/) with [CVE-2024-9379](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/cves/CVE-2024-9379/). Attackers used stolen admin credentials, webshells, and reconnaissance tools like Obelisk and GoGo Scanner to maintain persistence and attempt lateral movement, including targeting a vulnerable Jenkins server. Victim organizations detected the activity through anomalous user account creation, endpoint protection alerts, and log analysis, mitigating further damage by replacing compromised virtual machines. While rapid detection prevented successful follow-on activity in most cases, the exfiltration of admin credentials highlights ongoing risks.

## Microsoft Analysis and Additional OSINT Context
In September 2024, CVE-2024-8963 and CVE-2024-8190 were added to the [Known Exploited Vulnerability (KEV) Catalog](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog?search_api_fulltext=CVE-2024-8190&field_date_added_wrapper=all&field_cve=&sort_by=field_date_added&items_per_page=20&url=) after an exploitation was reported by [FortiGuard Labs](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/0c0e8013). Ivanti quickly released a [security advisory](https://forums.ivanti.com/s/article/Security-Advisory-Ivanti-Cloud-Service-Appliance-CSA-CVE-2024-8190?language=de) addressing CVE-2024-8190. In October 2024, Researchers at FortiGuard Labs reported their findings on the sophisticated cyberattack that exploited these vulnerabilities where the attacker gained unauthorized access, escalated privileges, and executed malicious commands while maintaining persistence by creating rogue accounts and patching the exploited vulnerabilities. Additionally, the attackers used the compromised system as a proxy for further attacks, demonstrating advanced tactics and control. Upon the discovery of the additional vulnerabilities, CVE-2024-9380 and CVE-2024-9379 were added to the KEV, and Ivanti released an additional [security advisory](https://forums.ivanti.com/s/article/Security-Advisory-Ivanti-CSA-Cloud-Services-Appliance-CVE-2024-9379-CVE-2024-9380-CVE-2024-9381?language=de).

## Recommendations
Microsoft recommends the following actions to mitigate the risk of this threat
 
- [Upgrade to Ivanti CSA 5.0](https://forums.ivanti.com/s/article/CSA-5-0-Download). Please note that Ivanti CSA 4.6 is EOL and no longer receives patches or third-party libraries. Customers must upgrade to the latest version of the product for continued support.
- Turn on [cloud-delivered protection](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/configure-block-at-first-sight-microsoft-defender-antivirus?view=o365-worldwide) in Microsoft Defender Antivirus or its equivalent for your antivirus product to cover rapidly evolving attacker tools and techniques. Cloud-based machine learning protections block a majority of new and unknown variants.
- Turn on [tamper protection](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/prevent-changes-to-security-settings-with-tamper-protection?view=o365-worldwide) features to prevent attackers from stopping security services.
- Run [EDR in block mode](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/edr-in-block-mode?view=o365-worldwide) so that Microsoft Defender for Endpoint can block malicious artifacts, even when your non-Microsoft antivirus doesn’t detect the threat or when Microsoft Defender Antivirus is running in passive mode. EDR in block mode works behind the scenes to remediate malicious artifacts that are detected post-breach.
- Enable [investigation and remediation](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/automated-investigations?view=o365-worldwide) in full automated mode to allow Microsoft Defender for Endpoint to take immediate action on alerts to resolve breaches, significantly reducing alert volume.
- Use [device discovery](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/device-discovery?view=o365-worldwide) to increase your visibility into your network by finding unmanaged devices and onboarding them to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
- Use multi-factor authentication (MFA) to mitigate credential theft and prevent attacker access. Keep MFA always-on for privileged accounts and apply risk-based MFA for normal accounts. Consider transitioning to a passwordless primary authentication method, such as Azure MFA, certificates, or Windows Hello for Business.
- To help block lateral movements:

    - [Block process creations originating from PsExec and WMI commands](https://docs.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction#block-process-creations-originating-from-psexec-and-wmi-commands)
    - [Block executable files from running unless they meet a prevalence, age, or trusted list criterion](https://docs.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction#block-executable-files-from-running-unless-they-meet-a-prevalence-age-or-trusted-list-criterion)
    - [Block credential stealing from the Windows local security authority subsystem (lsass.exe)](https://docs.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction#block-credential-stealing-from-the-windows-local-security-authority-subsystem)

CISA and the FBI recommend the following steps to mitigate the risk of this threat: 

- Establish a baseline and maintain detailed logs of network traffic, account behavior, and software to assist in the identification of anomalies that may indicate malicious activity more quickly.
- Secure remote access tools by:
    - Implementing application controls to manage and control software execution, including allowlisting remote access programs.
    - Audit the network for systems using RDP, close unused RDP ports, and log RDP login attempts.
    - Enforce account lockouts after a specified number of attempts.
- If compromise is detected, CISA and the FBI recommend:
    - Quarantine or take offline potentially affected hosts.
    - Reimage compromised hosts.
    - Provision new account credentials.
    - Collect and review artifacts such as running processes/services, unusual authentications, and recent network connections.
    - More recommendations can be found in the original article: [Threat Actors Chained Vulnerabilities in Ivanti Cloud Service Applications.](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa25-022a)

## References

title: RID Hijacking Technique Utilized by Andariel Attack Group
content:
## Snapshot
AhnLab Security Intelligence Center (ASEC) has identified the Andariel attack group utilizing a malicious file and an open-source tool to execute an RID Hijacking attack.

## Description
RID Hijacking is a technique where the Relative Identifier (RID) value of a low-privilege account is modified to match that of a high-privilege account, like an administrator account, effectively granting the former administrative rights. The Andariel group (tracked by Microsoft as [Onyx Sleet](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/03ced82eecb35bdb459c47b7821b9b055d1dfa00b56dc1b06f59583bad8833c0)) uses this method to create a backdoor account, which is difficult to detect as it involves modifying the Security Account Manager (SAM) database. 

The attack process begins with the threat actor gaining SYSTEM privileges using tools like [PsExec](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0029/) or JuicyPotato. They then create a local user account, often hidden by appending a $ to the account name, which is not visible using standard commands but can be seen in the SAM registry. This account is added to the Remote Desktop Users and Administrators groups to facilitate remote access. 

The core of the RID Hijacking involves modifying the registry value of the account's RID in the SAM database to match that of the target account. The Andariel group uses a malicious file and an open-source tool, called CreateHiddenAccount, they created to perform these actions. The malicious file requires system privileges to function, while the open-source tool can operate with administrator privileges, using the regini.exe tool to modify registry permissions. 

The threat actor's behavior includes adding the created account to the registry, extracting related keys, and then deleting the account to minimize exposure. However, the account can be detected again after a system reboot.

## Microsoft Analysis and Additional OSINT Context
[In December 2024](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/14ca8afc), ASEC reported that the Andariel threat group resumed its attacks distributing SmallTiger malware to target Korean software solutions, including asset and document management tools. Similar to the RID Hijacking attack, the threat group configured infected systems for future Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) access and employed the open-source tool CreateHiddenAccount to add and conceal a backdoor account.

## Recommendations
Microsoft recommends the following mitigations to reduce the impact of this threat.

- Implement [strong access controls](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/business/security-101/what-is-access-control)  to secure sensitive information, detect if a breach has already occurred or is currently in action by suspicious emails or [login security](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/business/security-101/what-is-login-security) activity, and adopt [Zero Trust principles](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/business/security-101/what-is-zero-trust-architecture) to reduce time in breach detection. [Zero trust](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/zero-trust/zero-trust-overview) assumes that threats could be both external and internal and require verification at every access attempt.
- Limit access to personal data [using strong passwords](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/create-and-use-strong-passwords-c5cebb49-8c53-4f5e-2bc4-fe357ca048eb#:~:text=Create%20strong%20passwords&text=A%20strong%20password%20is:%2ccharacter%2c%20product%2c%20or%20organization.) and regularly update security settings.
- Enable [passwordless authentication methods](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-authentication-methods) available in [Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/whatis) (for example, [Windows Hello](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/hello-for-business/), [FIDO keys](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/how-to-enable-passkey-fido2), or Microsoft Authenticator) for accounts that support passwordless.
- Use [Microsoft Entra ID Protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-protection/overview-identity-protection) to help detect, investigate, and remediate identity-based risks like leaked credentials.
- Enforce MFA on all accounts and [require MFA](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/identity-protection/howto-identity-protection-configure-mfa-policy?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) from all devices.
- For accounts that still require passwords, use authenticator apps like Microsoft Authenticator for MFA. [Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/authentication/concept-authentication-methods?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) adds another layer of security over only using a password when a user signs in. Remove users excluded from MFA, and strictly [require MFA](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/identity-protection/howto-identity-protection-configure-mfa-policy?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) from all devices, in all locations, at all times. For MFA that uses authenticator apps, ensure that the app requires a code to be typed in where possible, as many intrusions where MFA was enabled still succeeded due to users clicking “Yes” on the prompt on their phones even when they were not at their [devices](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/authentication/how-to-mfa-number-match?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc).
- Separate privileged roles: Admin and user accounts should be distinct. Use [Privileged Identity Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/privileged-identity-management/pim-configure) or separate accounts for privileged tasks, limiting accounts with excessive permissions. Apply [Conditional Access](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/conditional-access/overview), especially for accounts with elevated roles.
- Practicing the [principle of least privilege and building credential hygiene](https://www.microsoft.com/security/blog/2022/05/09/ransomware-as-a-service-understanding-the-cybercrime-gig-economy-and-how-to-protect-yourself?ocid=magicti_ta_blog#defending-against-ransomware).
- Additional layers of protection may be applied with intrusion detection and prevention systems ([IDPS](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall/premium-features#idps)) using Azure Firewall Premium. [Perform network intrusion detection by using Azure Network Watcher and open-source tools.](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/network-watcher-intrusion-detection-open-source-tools) Use Azure Web Application Firewall ([WAF](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/web-application-firewall/overview?WT.mc_id=AZ-MVP-5000120)) to provide centralized protection of your web applications from common exploits and vulnerabilities.
- Configure insider risk management with [Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/business/risk-management/microsoft-purview-insider-risk-management). [Turn on Microsoft 365 audit logs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/audit-log-enable-disable?tabs=microsoft-purview-portal) to stay informed of actions taken by the insider risk management features. Additionally, attackers may attempt to hide evidence of the breach by disabling auditing features, clearing logs, or manipulating log files. Therefore, [verify the auditing status for your organization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/audit-log-enable-disable?tabs=microsoft-purview-portal#verify-the-auditing-status-for-your-organization) or [employ audit logging](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/compliance/assurance/assurance-audit-logging) detection, and view [best practices for managing auditing and security logging](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-10/security/threat-protection/security-policy-settings/manage-auditing-and-security-log). Read about [guidance on searching the audit log](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/audit-search?tabs=microsoft-purview-portal).

## Detections/Hunting Queries

### Microsoft Defender Antivirus
- [HackTool:PowerShell/PsExec](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=HackTool:PowerShell/PsExec.B!MTB&threatId=-2147161971)
- [HackTool:Win32/Psexec](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=HackTool:Win32/Psexec!mclg&threatId=-2147154212)
- [HackTool:Win32/JuicyPotato](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=HackTool:Win32/JuicyPotato.A&ThreatID=2147905851)
- [HackTool:Win64/JuicyPotato](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=HackTool:Win64/JuicyPotato&ThreatID=2147740472)
- [HackTool:Win32/Malgent!MSR](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=HackTool:Win32/Malgent!MSR&ThreatID=2147774372)

## References

title: Cyble Finds Thousands of Security Vendor Credentials on Dark Web
content:
## Snapshot
An investigation by Cyble revealed that account credentials from 13 major cybersecurity vendors have been leaked on the dark web, with some being sold for as little as $10.

## Description
The leaked credentials include both internal accounts and customer access, covering systems like Okta, AWS, Jira, GitHub, Microsoft Online, and Salesforce. These credentials, likely obtained from info-stealer malware logs, provide access to sensitive enterprise environments, development systems, and account management interfaces.
 
Cyble found credentials from both enterprise and consumer security companies, all of which have experienced data exposures since the start of the year. Many leaked accounts were tied to web console interfaces, SSO logins, and other web-facing systems, potentially giving threat actors access to critical systems. Additionally, company email addresses were associated with sensitive developer and product accounts, increasing the risk of substantial exposure.
 
The analysis highlights that leaked credentials, even if outdated or protected by additional security measures, can aid hackers in reconnaissance. Exposed URLs for management interfaces and other sensitive details provide attackers with insights into system infrastructure and potential vulnerabilities. According to Cyble, these findings underscore the significant risks posed by credential leaks in the cybersecurity industry.

## Recommendations
Microsoft recommends the following mitigations to reduce the impact of this threat. Check the recommendations card for the deployment status of monitored mitigations.

- Check your Office 365 email filtering settings to ensure you block spoofed emails, spam, and emails with malware. Use [Microsoft Defender for Office 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/defender-for-office-365?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) for enhanced phishing protection and coverage against new threats and polymorphic variants. Configure Microsoft Defender for Office 365 to [recheck links on click](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/safe-links-about?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) and [delete sent mail](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/zero-hour-auto-purge?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in response to newly acquired threat intelligence. Turn on [safe attachments policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/safe-attachments-policies-configure?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to check attachments to inbound email.
- Encourage users to use Microsoft Edge and other web browsers that support [SmartScreen](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/web-protection-overview?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc), which identifies and blocks malicious websites, including phishing sites, scam sites, and sites that host malware.
- Turn on [cloud-delivered protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/configure-block-at-first-sight-microsoft-defender-antivirus?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in Microsoft Defender Antivirus, or the equivalent for your antivirus product, to cover rapidly evolving attacker tools and techniques. Cloud-based machine learning protections block a majority of new and unknown variants.
- Enforce MFA on all accounts, remove users excluded from MFA, and strictly [require MFA](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/identity-protection/howto-identity-protection-configure-mfa-policy?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) from all devices, in all locations, at all times.
- Enable passwordless authentication methods (for example, Windows Hello, FIDO keys, or Microsoft Authenticator) for accounts that support passwordless. For accounts that still require passwords, use authenticator apps like Microsoft Authenticator for MFA. [Refer to this article](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/authentication/concept-authentication-methods?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) for the different authentication methods and features.
- For MFA that uses authenticator apps, ensure that the app requires a code to be typed in where possible, as many intrusions where MFA was enabled still succeeded due to users clicking “Yes” on the prompt on their phones even when they were not at their [devices](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/authentication/how-to-mfa-number-match?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc). Refer to [this article](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/authentication/concept-authentication-methods?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) for an example.
- Remind employees that enterprise or workplace credentials should not be stored in browsers or password vaults secured with personal credentials. Organizations can turn off password syncing in browser on managed devices using [Group Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/microsoft-edge-enterprise-sync#sync-group-policies?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc).

Microsoft Defender customers can [turn on attack surface reduction rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to prevent common attack techniques used in infostealer infections. Attack surface reduction rules are sweeping settings that stop entire classes of threats including, infostealers, credential theft, and ransomware. The following bullet points offer more guidance on specific mitigation advice:

- [Turn on PUA protection in block mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/detect-block-potentially-unwanted-apps-microsoft-defender-antivirus?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc)
- [Block executable files from running unless they meet a prevalence, age, or trusted list criterion](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-executable-files-from-running-unless-they-meet-a-prevalence-age-or-trusted-list-criterion)
- [Block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-execution-of-potentially-obfuscated-scripts)

## Detections/Hunting Queries

### Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
Alerts with the following titles in the security center can indicate threat activity on your network:
 
- Information stealing malware activity

title: PlushDaemon compromises supply chain of Korean VPN service
content:
## Snapshot
Researchers at ESET have identified a supply chain attack against a South Korean VPN provider perpetrated by a China-linked threat group named PlushDaemon.

## Description
PlushDaemon compromised the installer for the VPN software IPany, embedding a backdoor called SlowStepper alongside the legitimate application. SlowStepper is a highly modular malware, equipped with over 30 components for tasks such as data theft, system monitoring, and persistence.
 
The attack, which dates back to at least November 2023, was discovered in May 2024 when the malicious installer was found on the VPN provider's official website. ESET's analysis revealed that victims manually downloaded the compromised software, affecting entities such as a semiconductor firm and a software company in South Korea. PlushDaemon, active since at least 2019, has been observed conducting espionage activities against individuals and organizations in China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, South Korea, the United States, and New Zealand. The group specializes in hijacking software updates and exploiting web server vulnerabilities.
 
PlushDaemon's custom malware, SlowStepper, uses sophisticated techniques for command-and-control (C&C) communication, leveraging DNS queries to dynamically identify its servers. Its modular design, built with C++, Python, and Go, supports functions like system reconnaissance, audio and video recording, and browser data extraction. The malware also exploits Python scripts to execute customized tools for data collection and exfiltration.

## Microsoft Analysis and Additional OSINT Context
Software supply chain attacks are particularly impactful because they exploit trust relationships between software providers and their users. By compromising legitimate software or updates, attackers can bypass traditional security measures, as these malicious payloads often appear authentic and are delivered through trusted channels. Such attacks have a wide reach, potentially affecting all users of the compromised software, and can remain undetected for extended periods, allowing attackers to gather sensitive information or infiltrate critical systems. Further, the highly interconnected nature of modern software ecosystems amplifies the impact, as compromised software can serve as a stepping stone for lateral movement within organizations or for targeting other interconnected systems. This makes software supply chain attacks a preferred tactic for sophisticated threat actors seeking widespread access and long-term persistence.

Microsoft tracks a number of actors who have been observed conducting supply chain attacks including [North Korea-linked actors](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/c83adbd4) like [Citrine Sleet](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/740afa51582ebef367a7120efe99a535ba803f2169356580369a0fd680137145), [Diamond Sleet](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/b982c8daf198d93a2ff52b92b65c6284243aa6af91dda5edd1fe8ec5365918c5), and [Jade Sleet](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/5b9e6492c6f43b9e7a194d03c1781fe9881dd9dc0a7208f363133c696afcb485) and [Russia-linked actors](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/a82ac4d8) like [Seashell Blizzard](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/cf1e406a16835d56cf614430aea3962d7ed99f01ee3d9ee3048078288e5201bb) and [Midnight Blizzard](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/d825313b053efea45228ff1f4cb17c8b5433dcd2f86353e28be2d484ce874616).

## Recommendations
Microsoft recommends the following mitigations for related threats.

- Establish [best practices to secure software supply chain](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/concepts/security-best-practices).
- Conduct an [audit for packages and dependencies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/concepts/auditing-packages), analyzing the security of packages included in software projects.
- Configure [continuous access evaluation](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/conditional-access/concept-continuous-access-evaluation?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in your tenant.
- Invest in advanced anti-phishing solutions that monitor incoming emails and visited websites. [Microsoft Defender for Office](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender/microsoft-365-security-center-mdo?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) 365 brings together incident and alert management across email, devices, and identities, centralizing investigations for threats in email. To build resilience against phishing attacks in general, organizations can use [anti-phishing policies](https://docs.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/set-up-anti-phishing-policies?view=o365-worldwide) to enable mailbox intelligence settings, as well as configure impersonation protection settings for specific messages and sender domains. Enabling [SafeLinks](https://docs.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/safe-links?view=o365-worldwide) ensures real-time protection by scanning at time of delivery and at time of click.
- Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management Admins can conduct their own [Browser extensions assessment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-vulnerability-management/tvm-browser-extensions).

## Detections/Hunting Queries

### Microsoft Defender Antivirus
Microsoft Defender Antivirus detects threat components as the following malware:
 
- [Trojan:Win32/Wacatac](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=Trojan:Win32/Wacatac.B!ml)

## References
[PlushDaemon compromises supply chain of Korean VPN service](https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/plushdaemon-compromises-supply-chain-korean-vpn-service/). ESET (accessed 2025-01-22)

title: Cloudflare mitigated a record-breaking 5.6 Tbps DDoS attack
content:
#### Targeted Geolocations
- East Asia



## Snapshot
A Mirai-based botnet consisting of 13,000 compromised devices launched the largest DDoS attack on record, peaking at 5.6 terabits per second.

## Description
The attack, which was [UDP-based](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/ddos/udp-flood-ddos-attack/), targeted an internet service provider in Eastern Asia on October 29 and lasted 80 seconds. Despite its magnitude, the attack had no impact on the target and generated no alerts due to the autonomous detection and mitigation by Cloudflare. This surpassed the previous record of a 3.8 Tbps attack reported by Cloudflare in early October 2024. 

Hyper-volumetric DDoS attacks have been on the rise, with a significant increase in the frequency of attacks exceeding 1 Tbps in the fourth quarter of 2024. Attacks surpassing 100 million packets per second also grew, with some exceeding 1 billion packets per second. Despite the increase in large-scale attacks, most HTTP DDoS attacks remained small, not exceeding 50,000 requests per second, and the majority of network layer DDoS attacks did not go beyond 500 Mbps. 

Cloudflare also noted a trend towards shorter, more intense DDoS attacks, with the majority of HTTP and network layer DDoS attacks ending in less than 10 minutes. These blitz attacks often coincide with peak usage periods for maximum impact. Ransom DDoS attacks have also seen a significant increase, particularly during the fourth quarter and the Christmas holiday season. The most targeted regions in the last quarter of 2024 were China, the Philippines, and Taiwan, with the telecommunications, service providers, internet sector, and marketing and advertising industries being the most affected.

## Microsoft Analysis and Additional OSINT Context
Botnets, networks of compromised devices controlled by threat actors, have cemented their place as one of the most persistent and versatile cyber threats. Botnet activity is both increasing and increasingly impactful, with a [25% year-over-year surge](https://www.ustelecom.org/research/botnets2024/) in botnet activity in 2024 and a staggering economic impact of botnet-enabled cybercrime estimated at [approximately $600 billion annually](https://kpmg.com/nl/en/home/insights/2024/08/exploring-botnets-understanding-the-threat-landscape-and-building-ethical-awareness.html).

Mirai-based botnets remain among the most active and well-documented threats in the botnet ecosystem, particularly in the IoT and DDoS space. Recent campaigns include [a variant discovered by Akamai](https://sip.security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/bae0680c) in December 2024 that exploits a previously undocumented vulnerability in DigiEver DS-2105 Pro devices. This botnet also targets outdated TP-Link routers and network video recorders, employing ChaCha20 encryption and multi-architecture support to enhance its stealth and effectiveness. Another active Mirai-based botnet, the [Gorilla Botnet](https://sip.security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/0bcef023), issued over 300,000 DDoS commands in September, targeting sectors like government and telecommunications with UDP Floods and other methods. Additionally, [FortiGuard Labs reported](https://sip.security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/77c183a0) activity from the FICORA botnet, another Mirai strain, and the Kaiten-based CAPSAICIN botnet, both exploiting long-standing vulnerabilities in D-Link devices. These campaigns demonstrate how Mirai variants continue to adapt and pose significant risks, particularly to IoT devices and industries reliant on legacy or unpatched systems.

## Recommendations
Microsoft recommends the following mitigations to reduce the impact of botnets.
 
- [Restrict automatic prompts](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/automatic-file-download-notifications-in-windows-dc73c9c9-1b4c-a8b7-8d8b-b471736bb5a0) for non-user-initiated file downloads.
- [Enable Safe Links](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchange/enable-safelinksrule?view=exchange-ps) protection for links in email messages.
- [Enable Safe Attachments](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchange/set-safeattachmentrule?view=exchange-ps) in block mode.
- Enable [Zero-hour auto purge (ZAP)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/zero-hour-auto-purge) in Office 365 to quarantine sent mail in response to newly-acquired threat intelligence and retroactively neutralize malicious phishing, spam, or malware messages that have already been delivered to mailboxes.
- Run endpoint detection and response [(EDR) in block mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/edr-in-block-mode) so that Microsoft Defender for Endpoint can block malicious artifacts, even when your non-Microsoft antivirus does not detect the threat or when Microsoft Defender Antivirus is running in passive mode.

title: "Crazy Evil" Cryptoscam Gang: Unmasking a Global Threat in 2024
content:
## Snapshot
Researchers from Insikt Group have uncovered the activities of Crazy Evil, a highly flexible Russian-speaking cybercriminal group that specializes in identity fraud, cryptocurrency theft, and information stealer malware.

## Description
Crazy Evil operates through a network of traffers, who are social engineering experts that redirect legitimate traffic to malicious phishing pages. The group is organized into six subteams—AVLAND, TYPED, DELAND, ZOOMLAND, DEFI, and KEVLAND—each running scams tailored to specific victim profiles. 
 
Crazy Evil primarily targets cryptocurrency users, influencers, and gaming personalities by creating highly convincing spearphishing campaigns. The group uses infostealer malware such as Stealc, Atomic macOS Stealer (AMOS), and Angel Drainer to compromise victims' devices and steal digital assets. Their phishing scams have been linked to major attacks on social media, often exploiting platforms like Telegram and Discord to distribute malicious links.
 
Since its emergence in 2021, Crazy Evil has generated millions of dollars in illicit revenue and has infected tens of thousands of devices globally. The group actively promotes its services on dark web forums like Lolz.Guru and YouHack, offering training and resources to aspiring traffers. Their methods include hardware wallet attacks, address poisoning, and fully undetectable (FUD) malware deployment.
 
Insikt Group reports that Crazy Evil has remained undetected for nearly four years, continuously adapting its techniques. The group has expanded beyond targeting job seekers to exploiting the decentralized finance (DeFi) ecosystem, making it a growing threat to cryptocurrency security. Their ability to rapidly adjust to security measures and recruit new affiliates suggests their operations will persist, posing a significant risk to individuals and organizations in the digital asset space.

## Recommendations
Microsoft recommends the following mitigations to reduce the impact of this threat. Check the recommendations card for the deployment status of monitored mitigations.

- Check your Office 365 email filtering settings to ensure you block spoofed emails, spam, and emails with malware. Use [Microsoft Defender for Office 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/defender-for-office-365?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) for enhanced phishing protection and coverage against new threats and polymorphic variants. Configure Microsoft Defender for Office 365 to [recheck links on click](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/safe-links-about?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) and [delete sent mail](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/zero-hour-auto-purge?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in response to newly acquired threat intelligence. Turn on [safe attachments policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/safe-attachments-policies-configure?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to check attachments to inbound email.
- Encourage users to use Microsoft Edge and other web browsers that support [SmartScreen](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/web-protection-overview?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc), which identifies and blocks malicious websites, including phishing sites, scam sites, and sites that host malware.
- Turn on [cloud-delivered protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/configure-block-at-first-sight-microsoft-defender-antivirus?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in Microsoft Defender Antivirus, or the equivalent for your antivirus product, to cover rapidly evolving attacker tools and techniques. Cloud-based machine learning protections block a majority of new and unknown variants.
- Enforce MFA on all accounts, remove users excluded from MFA, and strictly [require MFA](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/identity-protection/howto-identity-protection-configure-mfa-policy?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) from all devices, in all locations, at all times.
- Enable passwordless authentication methods (for example, Windows Hello, FIDO keys, or Microsoft Authenticator) for accounts that support passwordless. For accounts that still require passwords, use authenticator apps like Microsoft Authenticator for MFA. [Refer to this article](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/authentication/concept-authentication-methods?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) for the different authentication methods and features.
- For MFA that uses authenticator apps, ensure that the app requires a code to be typed in where possible, as many intrusions where MFA was enabled still succeeded due to users clicking “Yes” on the prompt on their phones even when they were not at their [devices](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/authentication/how-to-mfa-number-match?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc). Refer to [this article](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/authentication/concept-authentication-methods?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) for an example.
- Remind employees that enterprise or workplace credentials should not be stored in browsers or password vaults secured with personal credentials. Organizations can turn off password syncing in browser on managed devices using [Group Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/microsoft-edge-enterprise-sync#sync-group-policies?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc).

Microsoft Defender customers can [turn on attack surface reduction rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to prevent common attack techniques used in infostealer infections. Attack surface reduction rules are sweeping settings that stop entire classes of threats including, infostealers, credential theft, and ransomware. The following bullet points offer more guidance on specific mitigation advice:

- [Turn on PUA protection in block mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/detect-block-potentially-unwanted-apps-microsoft-defender-antivirus?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc)
- [Block executable files from running unless they meet a prevalence, age, or trusted list criterion](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-executable-files-from-running-unless-they-meet-a-prevalence-age-or-trusted-list-criterion)
- [Block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-execution-of-potentially-obfuscated-scripts)

## Detections/Hunting Queries

### Microsoft Defender Antivirus
Microsoft Defender Antivirus detects threat components as the following malware:
 
- [Spyware:Win32/Stealc](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=Spyware:Win32/Stealc)

title: Fortinet Zero-Day CVE-2024-55591 Exposed: Super-Admin Access Risk
content:
## Snapshot
A critical zero-day vulnerability, [CVE-2024-55591](https://sip.security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/cves/CVE-2024-55591), has been discovered in Fortinet's FortiOS and FortiProxy products, which is currently being actively exploited by attackers.

## Description
This flaw, rated with a CVSSv3 score of 9.8, allows attackers to bypass authentication and potentially obtain super-admin privileges due to weaknesses in the Node.js WebSocket module. The vulnerability affects FortiOS versions 7.0.0 through 7.0.16 and FortiProxy versions 7.0.0 through 7.0.19 and 7.2.0 through 7.2.12. 

Attackers are sending malicious WebSocket requests to bypass authentication controls, targeting administrative accounts by guessing or brute-forcing usernames. Once inside, they can create administrative or local user accounts, modify firewall policies, and establish SSL VPN tunnels to penetrate internal networks.

## Recommendations
The source recommends:

**Upgrade to the latest secure versions of FortiOS or FortiProxy to mitigate vulnerabilities.**  
Organizations using affected versions should prioritize upgrading to FortiOS version 7.0.17 or later and FortiProxy to versions 7.0.20 or 7.2.13. Up-to-date versions ensure the system is protected against known exploits. Fortinet offers tools and resources to assist with the upgrade process, accessible via their official website.

**Implement immediate mitigations for protection if an upgrade is not feasible.**  
To reduce the risk of exploitation until an upgrade can be performed, consider the following measures:

- **Disable HTTP/HTTPS Administrative Interfaces.**  
Limiting the exposure of management interfaces to the internet helps protect against unauthorized access.
- **Restrict access to administrative interfaces.**  
Use local-in policies to allow access only from trusted IP addresses, effectively reducing the attack surface.
- **Use non-standard admin usernames.**  
Avoid predictable or default usernames for administrative accounts to make brute-force attacks more challenging.

## References

title: 2024 macOS Malware Review Infostealers, Backdoors, and APT Campaigns Targeting the Enterprise
content:
## Snapshot
In 2024, there was a significant increase in malware campaigns targeting macOS users in enterprise settings. Threat actors utilized various tactics, including infostealers disguised as business apps, sophisticated modular backdoors, and advanced persistent threat (APT) activity, to compromise organizations and steal sensitive data.

## Description
The Amos Atomic infostealer family, which used AppleScript to phish for credentials, and the macOS.Bkdr.Activator backdoor, distributed through cracked apps, were among the threats. The latter installed a Python runtime for command execution and used persistence agents. Additionallly, a group known as APT41, and tracked by Microsoft as [Brass Typhoon](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/f0aaa62bfbaf3739bb92106688e6a00fc05eafc0d4158b0e389b4078112d37c6), utilized LightSpy malware to target Indian users. The malware offers a modular surveillance toolset with file theft and data harvesting capabilities, and employs certificate pinning for evasion. 

North Korean state-sponsored groups deployed BeaverTail malware, which targeted job seekers on professional platforms with trojanized applications. The BlueNoroff APT, tracked by Microsoft as [Sapphire Sleet](https:/security.microsoft.com/intel-profiles/45e4b0c21eecf6012661ef6df36a058a0ada1c6be74d8d2011ea3699334b06d1), targeted cryptocurrency users with the code-signed and notarized ToDoSwift and Hidden Risk malware. Hidden Risk droppers injected code into the host's zshenv file for persistence and downloaded a second-stage backdoor capable of host reconnaissance and command execution. The HZ RAT backdoor, masquerading as an OpenVPN Connect installer, stole data from chat apps like DingTalk and WeChat. 

Other threats included CloudChat, an infostealer that monitored clipboards and exfiltrated data from users outside China, and NotLockBit ransomware, which was designed for file encryption and data exfiltration. Additionally, RustyAttr, a suspected DPRK malware, used extended attributes to hide malicious code within signed and notarized applications, often using decoy PDFs to backdoor targets. These threats underscored the increasing focus on macOS as a target for sophisticated attacks and the exploitation of macOS defense gaps.

## Microsoft Analysis and Additional OSINT Context
Microsoft has documented the targeting of macOS users and previously highlighted [LightSpy malware](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/a1778f1d) in campaigns focused on Southern Asia. The campaign features a Windows-based surveillance tool called DeepData, with 12 plugins enabling advanced data theft from apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal, Outlook, and password managers. DeepData's capabilities include collecting browser credentials, system data, email communications, and audio recordings, with a focus on Southeast Asian entities such as political figures, activists, and journalists. The group has also enhanced its infrastructure with new SSL certificates, improving security and longevity. These advancements highlight the increasing sophistication of LightSpy and DeepData, making them a persistent threat that demands robust cybersecurity measures.

Microsoft has also reported on Sapphire Sleet's targeting of cryptocurrency users through the deployment of [TodoSwift malware](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/c6573902). This malware disguises itself as a legitimate app named TodoTasks, appears to download a PDF while secretly executing a malicious binary. The malware uses a Swift/SwiftUI-based dropper to download and launch its payload, leveraging a Google Drive URL—similar to other DPRK malware tactics. The malware is likely used for financially motivated cyber espionage, continuing North Korea's trend of targeting macOS systems. Microsoft has analyzed recent incidents and insights from the security community to identify [recent OSINT trends of North Korean threat actors](https://security.microsoft.com/intel-explorer/articles/87adc2a0), including Sapphire Sleet, and offer recommendations for effective defense against these threats.

## Recommendations
Apply these mitigations to reduce the impact of this threat. Check the recommendations card for the deployment status of monitored mitigations.
 
- Use [Microsoft Defender Antivirus](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/microsoft-defender-antivirus-windows?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to protect from this threat.
- Turn on  and automatic sample submission on Microsoft Defender Antivirus. These capabilities use artificial intelligence and machine learning to quickly identify and stop new and unknown threats.
- Educate users about [protecting personal and business information](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/business/security-101/what-is-email-security?ocid=magicti_ta_abbreviatedmktgpage) in social media, filtering unsolicited communication, identifying lures in spear-phishing email and watering holes, and reporting reconnaissance attempts and other suspicious activity.
- Educate users about [preventing malware infections](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/business/security-101/what-is-malware?ocid=magicti_ta_abbreviatedmktgpage), such as ignoring or deleting unsolicited and unexpected emails or attachments sent through instant messaging applications or social networks.
- Turn on [tamper protection for macOS](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/tamperprotection-macos?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint to prevent malicious changes to security settings.
- Encourage users to practice good [credential hygeine](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/business/security-101/what-is-login-security?ocid=magicti_ta_abbreviatedmktgpage) and turn on the Microsoft Defender Firewall to prevent malware infection and stifle propagation.
- Take immediate action to address malicious activity on the impacted device. If malicious code has been launched, the attacker has likely taken complete control of the device. Immediately isolate the system and perform a reset of credentials and tokens. Investigate the device timeline for indications of lateral movement activities using one of the compromised accounts. Check for additional tools that attackers might have dropped to enable credential access, lateral movement, and other attack activities.
- To protect against initial compromise, enable [Safe Links](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/safe-links-about?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) and [Safe Attachment](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/safe-attachments-about?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) policies in Defender for Office 365
- Enable [real-time protection for macOS](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/mac-preferences?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#enforcement-level-for-antivirus-engine) in Microsoft Defender Antivirus.
- Enable [real-time behavior monitoring for macOS](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/mac-preferences?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#enabledisable-behavior-monitoring) in Microsoft Defender Antivirus.
- Run endpoint detection and response [(EDR) in block mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/edr-in-block-mode?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) so that Microsoft Defender for Endpoint can block malicious artifacts, even when your non-Microsoft antivirus does not detect the threat or when Microsoft Defender Antivirus is running in passive mode. EDR in block mode works behind the scenes to remediate malicious artifacts that are detected post-breach.

## Detections/Hunting Queries

### Microsoft Defender Antivirus
Microsoft Defender Antivirus detects threat components as the following malware:
 
- [Trojan:MacOS/Multiverze](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=Trojan:MacOS/Multiverze)
- [Trojan:MacOS/NukeSped!MTB](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=Trojan:MacOS/Nukesped!MTB)

## References

title: TMPN (Skuld) Stealer: The dark side of open source
content:
## Snapshot
The Skuld malware, also known as TMPN Stealer, is a Golang-based information stealer that emerged in May 2023, attributed to a developer named "Deathined."

## Description
Distributed via malicious links and compromised websites, it targets global systems, with its configuration heavily inspired by open-source projects.
 
Skuld begins by loading configurations, including Discord webhooks and cryptocurrency wallet addresses, for data exfiltration. The malware establishes persistence through Windows registry keys and evades detection by hiding its processes, disabling Windows Defender, and blocking connections to antivirus-related sites. It also employs UAC bypass techniques to elevate its privileges.
 
The malware focuses on Discord, injecting JavaScript payloads to harvest user credentials, 2FA codes, and account activity. It also compromises cryptocurrency wallets like Exodus and Atomic by tampering with their archive files. Beyond this, Skuld collects extensive system information, browser data, and sensitive user files, packaging them into encrypted archives for exfiltration.
 
Additional capabilities include stealing game session data from platforms like Steam and Minecraft, targeting browser extensions for cryptocurrency wallets, and using a clipper to replace copied cryptocurrency addresses with the attacker’s BTC wallet. Despite its aggressive data collection methods, one noted sample lacked a functional server link for exfiltrated data, limiting its operational impact.
 
According to Acronis, Skuld demonstrates how cybercriminals can repurpose open-source tools to create sophisticated malware that targets popular platforms like Discord and cryptocurrency services, exploiting their widespread use for effective information theft.

## Recommendations
Microsoft recommends the following mitigations to reduce the impact of this threat.
 
- Turn on [cloud-delivered protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/linux-preferences) in Microsoft Defender Antivirus or the equivalent for your antivirus product to cover rapidly evolving attacker tools and techniques. Cloud-based machine learning protections block a majority of new and unknown threats.
- Run [EDR in block mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/edr-in-block-mode?view=o365-worldwide?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) so that Microsoft Defender for Endpoint can block malicious artifacts, even when your non-Microsoft antivirus does not detect the threat or when Microsoft Defender Antivirus is running in passive mode. EDR in block mode works behind the scenes to remediate malicious artifacts that are detected post-breach.
- Allow [investigation and remediation](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/automated-investigations?view=o365-worldwide?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in full automated mode to allow Microsoft Defender for Endpoint to take immediate action on alerts to resolve breaches, significantly reducing alert volume.
- [Enable](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/enable-controlled-folders) controlled folder access.
- Ensure that [tamper protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/prevent-changes-to-security-settings-with-tamper-protection#how-do-i-configure-or-manage-tamper-protection) is enabled in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
- Enable [network protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/enable-network-protection) in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
- Follow the credential hardening recommendations in the [on-premises credential theft overview](https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/9382203e-5155-4b5e-af74-21562b1004d5/analystreport) to defend against common credential theft techniques like LSASS access.
- [Enable](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference#block-credential-stealing-from-the-windows-local-security-authority-subsystem) LSA protection.

## Detections/Hunting Queries

### Microsoft Defender Antivirus
Microsoft Defender Antivirus detects threat components as the following malware:
 
- Trojan:Win64/SkuldStealer!MTB

title: Android Malware in DONOT APT Operations
content:
## Snapshot
CYFIRMA researchers have uncovered a malicious application, Tanzeem, attributed to the Indian APT group "DONOT."

## Description
The app, disguised as a chat platform, appears to target specific individuals or groups of interest, potentially serving Indian national intelligence purposes. Two nearly identical samples of the app were analyzed, collected in October and December, with minimal differences in their user interface.
 
Despite its appearance, the app does not function as a chat tool. Once installed and granted necessary permissions, it shuts down, suggesting its primary intent is covert data collection. The app misuses the OneSignal library, commonly used for legitimate push notifications, to deliver phishing links. This marks the first observed instance of DONOT leveraging OneSignal for malicious purposes.
 
The app requests dangerous permissions, enabling access to sensitive information such as call logs, contacts, SMS messages, and device storage. It can also extract precise location data, monitor device movement, and capture user credentials. Collected data is exfiltrated to a command-and-control (C2) server via embedded URLs and Appspot domains.
 
CYFIRMA's technical analysis of the app's code reveals modules designed to exploit accessibility settings, handle permissions, and even record screens. These features highlight the app's ability to operate stealthily while gathering extensive intelligence from compromised devices.

## Microsoft Analysis and Additional OSINT Context
The [DONOT group](https://www.welivesecurity.com/2022/01/18/donot-go-do-not-respawn/), also known as APT-C-35 or VICEROY TIGER, is a highly sophisticated threat group with ties to India, active since at least 2016. Initially targeting diverse sectors across multiple countries, their focus has shifted primarily to entities in Pakistan, particularly government and security organizations. The DoNot Team's campaigns are motivated by espionage and generally culminate in the collection and exfiltration of data. This group is known for deploying spear-phishing campaigns, often utilizing malicious Microsoft Office documents and Android-targeted malware, as well as phishing schemes designed to steal user credentials.

## Recommendations
- Only install applications from trusted sources and official stores.
- If a device is no longer receiving updates, strongly consider replacing it with a new device.
- Use mobile solutions such as [Microsoft Defender for Endpoint on Android](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/microsoft-defender-endpoint-android?view=o365-worldwide)to detect malicious applications
    - Always keep Install unknown apps disabled on the Android device to prevent apps from being installed from unknown sources.
- Evaluate whether [Microsoft Defender for Internet of Things (IoT)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-iot/organizations/overview) services are applicable to your IoT environment.

## Detections/Hunting Queries

### Microsoft Defender Antivirus
Microsoft Defender Antivirus detects threat components as the following malware:
 
- Trojan:AndroidOS/Kylk

title: MintsLoader: StealC and BOINC Delivery
content:
#### Targeted Geolocations
- United States  
- Western Europe  
- Northern Europe  
- Southern Europe



#### Targeted Industries
- Energy  
    - Electricity  
    - Oil & Natural Gas



## Snapshot
In January 2025, eSentire’s Threat Response Unit identified a campaign leveraging MintsLoader, a PowerShell-based malware loader, to deliver payloads such as StealC and the BOINC client.

## Description
The infection begins with spam emails containing links to malicious JScript files, which execute PowerShell commands to retrieve and execute the loader. MintsLoader employs sophisticated techniques like Domain Generation Algorithms (DGA) and anti-virtual machine checks to evade detection.
 
Once executed, MintsLoader retrieves and delivers StealC, an information-stealing malware that targets sensitive data from web browsers, crypto wallets, and email clients. StealC’s final stage involves downloading its payload from a file hosting site, executing it, and exfiltrating data to a command-and-control (C2) server. The malware is re-engineered from Arkei Stealer and has been sold as Malware-as-a-Service (MaaS) since 2023.
 
StealC employs numerous evasion techniques, including anti-debugging checks, encrypted strings, and system profile analysis. For instance, it terminates execution if certain system attributes—like resolution, memory size, or processor cores—indicate a sandbox environment. Additionally, the malware avoids running on systems with language settings from specific countries, such as Russia or Ukraine.
 
The campaign has primarily targeted industries like energy, legal services, and oil and gas in the U.S. and Europe. The use of advanced obfuscation, stealthy delivery mechanisms, and modular design highlights the evolving sophistication of modern cyber threats.

## Recommendations
Microsoft recommends the following mitigations to reduce the impact of this threat. Check the recommendations card for the deployment status of monitored mitigations.

- Check your Office 365 email filtering settings to ensure you block spoofed emails, spam, and emails with malware. Use [Microsoft Defender for Office 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/defender-for-office-365?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) for enhanced phishing protection and coverage against new threats and polymorphic variants. Configure Microsoft Defender for Office 365 to [recheck links on click](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/safe-links-about?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) and [delete sent mail](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/zero-hour-auto-purge?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in response to newly acquired threat intelligence. Turn on [safe attachments policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/safe-attachments-policies-configure?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to check attachments to inbound email.
- Encourage users to use Microsoft Edge and other web browsers that support [SmartScreen](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/web-protection-overview?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc), which identifies and blocks malicious websites, including phishing sites, scam sites, and sites that host malware.
- Turn on [cloud-delivered protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/configure-block-at-first-sight-microsoft-defender-antivirus?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) in Microsoft Defender Antivirus, or the equivalent for your antivirus product, to cover rapidly evolving attacker tools and techniques. Cloud-based machine learning protections block a majority of new and unknown variants.
- Enforce MFA on all accounts, remove users excluded from MFA, and strictly [require MFA](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/identity-protection/howto-identity-protection-configure-mfa-policy?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) from all devices, in all locations, at all times.
- Enable passwordless authentication methods (for example, Windows Hello, FIDO keys, or Microsoft Authenticator) for accounts that support passwordless. For accounts that still require passwords, use authenticator apps like Microsoft Authenticator for MFA. [Refer to this article](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/authentication/concept-authentication-methods?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) for the different authentication methods and features.
- For MFA that uses authenticator apps, ensure that the app requires a code to be typed in where possible, as many intrusions where MFA was enabled still succeeded due to users clicking “Yes” on the prompt on their phones even when they were not at their [devices](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/authentication/how-to-mfa-number-match?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc). Refer to [this article](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/authentication/concept-authentication-methods?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) for an example.
- Remind employees that enterprise or workplace credentials should not be stored in browsers or password vaults secured with personal credentials. Organizations can turn off password syncing in browser on managed devices using [Group Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/microsoft-edge-enterprise-sync#sync-group-policies?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc).

Microsoft Defender customers can [turn on attack surface reduction rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc) to prevent common attack techniques used in infostealer infections. Attack surface reduction rules are sweeping settings that stop entire classes of threats including, infostealers, credential theft, and ransomware. The following bullet points offer more guidance on specific mitigation advice:

- [Turn on PUA protection in block mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/detect-block-potentially-unwanted-apps-microsoft-defender-antivirus?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc)
- [Block executable files from running unless they meet a prevalence, age, or trusted list criterion](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-executable-files-from-running-unless-they-meet-a-prevalence-age-or-trusted-list-criterion)
- [Block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference?ocid=magicti_ta_learndoc#block-execution-of-potentially-obfuscated-scripts)

## Detections/Hunting Queries

### Microsoft Defender Antivirus
Microsoft Defender Antivirus detects threat components as the following malware:
 
- [Trojan:JS/Obfuse](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=Trojan:JS/Obfuse)
- [Trojan:Win32/LummaStealer](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=Trojan:Win32/LummaStealer!pz)

### Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
Alerts with the following titles in the security center can indicate threat activity on your network:
 
- Information stealing malware activity
